## Merge Notes

This document merges two research reports on the same question. Run 2's report (`RESEARCH-REPORT-review-panel-unification-run2.md`, 5,098 lines) is the base. Run 1's report (4,476 lines) contributes the blocks that carry the `R1-` id prefix. The merge followed `adversarial/refactor-plan.md` (changes M-00 to M-30) in the compare folder `.dev/tasks/to-do/COMPARE-review-panel-run1-vs-run2-20261114/`; Section 10.B lists every compare artifact.

**(a) Status: `partial`.** The compare debate examined 234 diff points (56 structural, 97 content, 63 contradictions, 18 promoted shared assumptions; `diff-analysis.md` Summary, `debate-points.md`).

| Measure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Points resolved (both advocates name the same winner, `Both (merge)` included) | 220 of 234 | `partials/scoring-matrix.md`, Convergence Assessment |
| Points both advocates call open (undecidable by the evidence; owner decision) | 6: X-040, X-056, X-058, C-060, X-041, X-057 | same |
| Points where the advocates still differ after Round 2 | 8: 3 real label disputes on the core shape (C-005, C-076, X-051) and 5 Medium/Low rows where one advocate's explicit Round 1 exception was not mirrored by the other (C-053, C-065, S-044, C-014, C-025) | same; `partials/convergence-r2.md` |
| Strict convergence (resolved points only) | 94.0% (220 of 234); 96.6% if the 6 both-open points are counted as agreement; 82.5% after Round 1; threshold 80% | `partials/matrix.json` (`strict` = 0.94017); `partials/scoring-matrix.md` |
| Points won (strict tally) | Variant 1 (run 1) 33, Variant 2 (run 2) 123, Both (merge) 64, Neither 0 | `partials/scoring-matrix.md` |
| Taxonomy coverage gate | PASS (L1 50 points, L2 126, L3 58, all addressed in both rounds) | same |
| Invariant probe gate | BLOCKS: 7 HIGH-severity UNADDRESSED invariants; status BLOCKED_BY_INVARIANTS; depth `standard` has no Round 3 | `invariant-probe.md` Summary |

How the 8 split points are read in this document (refactor-plan rule 4, applied to the regenerated matrix). C-005, C-076 and X-051 are a dispute about labels only on the core shape: the run 1 advocate holds BOTH (run 1's superset core kept as the documented one-engine target), the run 2 advocate holds "Variant 2 governing, run 1 detail carried" (`partials/r2-advocate-V1.md:167`; `partials/r2-advocate-V2.md:176`). Both positions are stated where the core shape is discussed (3.6, 7.4). The other 5 are Medium or Low rows where one advocate's explicit Round 1 exception was not mirrored by the other advocate (run 1 advocate: `partials/r1-advocate-V1.md`, "Inherited verdicts and exceptions"; run 2 advocate: `partials/r1-advocate-V2.md`, "Inherited points and exceptions" and its cluster table): C-053 (invalid-block unit of loss): run 1 advocate Variant 1, 65% (`partials/r1-advocate-V1.md:247`); run 2 advocate Variant 2, its CL-02 cluster verdict, no exception for C-053 (`partials/r1-advocate-V2.md:94`). C-065 (blocking predicate and severity vocabulary): run 1 advocate Variant 1, 55% (`partials/r1-advocate-V1.md:249`); run 2 advocate Variant 2, its CL-04 cluster verdict (`partials/r1-advocate-V2.md:96`). S-044 (post-debate re-rating of options): run 1 advocate Variant 1, 55% (`partials/r1-advocate-V1.md:262`); run 2 advocate Variant 2, its CL-17 cluster verdict (`partials/r1-advocate-V2.md:109`). C-014 (future consumers, PR code review and rf-qa): run 1 advocate Variant 1, 55% (`partials/r1-advocate-V1.md:259`); run 2 advocate Both, 60% (`partials/r1-advocate-V2.md:279`). C-025 (reflect memory writes): run 1 advocate Variant 2, 70% (`partials/r1-advocate-V1.md:254`); run 2 advocate MERGE, its CL-09 cluster verdict (`partials/r1-advocate-V2.md:101`). The matrix (`partials/scoring-matrix.md`, `partials/matrix.json`) applies each advocate's Round 1 exception list over the inherited cluster label (R25-INV-004); with it, C-010 and C-018 are Variant 1, C-017 is Variant 2, and C-020, C-021 and C-024 are Both (merge) for both advocates. The first line of `partials/consensus-summary.md` still reads "224 of 234 = 0.957" and "10 points still disputed"; the regenerated figures are 220 resolved, 226 counting the both-open points (0.966, `partials/convergence-r2.md`) and 8 split (R25-INV-016).

The base was chosen by the debate tiebreaker: the combined scores were run 1 0.8845 and run 2 0.8620, a margin of 2.5% (below the 5% threshold), and at tiebreaker level 1 run 2 won 123 of 234 points against run 1's 33, with 64 points Both (merge) (`base-selection.md`, Combined Scoring).

**(b) What is in this document and how to read it.**

- Base text (run 2) keeps its section numbers, its ids and its line-number citations. Each block carries an HTML comment naming its source: `Base (original)`, `Base (original, modified) — <reason>` for an in-place correction, `Variant 1, Section <n> (lines a-b) — merged per Change #<M-nn>` for a carried run 1 block, or `new text — merged per Change #<M-nn>` for text written by the merge.
- Run 1 blocks are added as numbered subsections at the end of the section they belong to: 2.10 (current state), 3.6 (target state), 4.7 and 4.8 (gap rows; contradictions and track coverage), 5.6 (external findings), 6.13 (conflict blocks, with the disposition table 6.13.0 at its head), 7.4 (run 1 recommendation and architecture, the recorded one-engine alternative), 8.3 to 8.8 (value inventory, migration content, no-regression gates, persisted-format rules, branch-structure constraint, risk inputs and checklist), 9.11 (open questions) and 10.A (evidence trail). Run 1's own section numbers appear in carried headings as `R1 n.m`.
- Where a carried run 1 block and the base disagree, the base governs unless a verified fact says otherwise; each such case is a row of Appendix C. Section 7.0.2 records which of run 2's 15 adjudicated outcomes the compare debate left unchanged and which it changed or reopened.
- New material from the compare: 7.0.2 (status of the 15 outcomes), 9.12 (open items raised by the compare debate), 10.B (compare artifacts), Appendix C (contradiction register, all 63 X rows), Appendix D (the 32-row invariant probe), Appendix E (corrections applied, and counts with units) and Appendix F (provenance index).

**(c) Owner decisions already made (context, not findings).**

- The shared core lives in `src/superclaude/cli/review/`, with thin modules.
- Branch names use the form `feat_review-panel/<name>` (the git-ref constraint that follows from this is in 8.7).
- Stacked pull requests are a matter for the later plan.
- The newer commits of the tasklist branch (newest `e2f2ac268`) are folded in later; neither report read them.
- Pull requests go only to `IronbellyOrg/IronClaude`, through `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3`.

**(d) Id rule.**

- Ids that exist in the base (run 2) are written without a prefix.
- Every id inside a block carried from run 1 carries the prefix `R1-`, for example `R1-D6`, `R1-C-17`, `R1-ENS-1`, `R1-INV-014`, `R1-G2`, `R1-M1-08`, `R1-V-001`. The prefixed families are run 1's debate-row ids (`R1-C13-22`), its own debate diff-point ids (`R1-C-nnn`, `R1-X-nnn`, `R1-S-nnn`, `R1-A-nnn`, `R1-U-nnn`; run 2 and the compare use the same shapes for other points), constraints and conflict shorthand (`R1-C1`..`R1-C14`, `R1-C01`..`R1-C20`), conflicts `R1-C-nn`, questions `R1-Q-nn`, owner items `R1-O-n`, `R1-OD-n`, hypotheses `R1-H-A`..`R1-H-C` and `R1-Hn`, web files `R1-W01`..`R1-W04`, defects `R1-Dn`, `R1-D-nn` and run 1's "Decision D-1" (`R1-D-1`; run 2's D-1 is a defect), log ids `R1-G-nn`, gates `R1-Gn` and `R1-G-all`, `R1-G-bench`, `R1-G-exit`, `R1-G-new`, `R1-G-pr`, `R1-G-replay`, `R1-G-skills`, `R1-G-sync`, gap rows `R1-BL-nn`, `R1-MS-nn`, `R1-ENS-n`, `R1-DOC-nn`, `R1-OPEN-nn`, success criteria `R1-SC-n`, constraints `R1-K-n`, migration steps `R1-M1-nn`..`R1-M4-nn`, tracks `R1-M1`..`R1-M4` (run 2's M1-M10 are moves), scope slices `R1-S00`..`R1-S05` (run 2's S02 is another folder), `R1-F-n`, inventory rows `R1-V-nnn`, exposures `R1-Xn`, `R1-A-nn`, invariants `R1-INV-nnn`, research files `R1-Rnn` and conditional items `R1-CI-n`.
- A range whose two ends belong to one family is written with both ends prefixed, for example `R1-D1..R1-D16`.
- Run 1's closed items (its list in 9.11, every `GQ C-nn` or `GQ:C-nn` reference and every `C-nn` after the words "closed item") are renamed `R1-CLS-nn`, so a closed item is never read as a run 1 conflict `R1-C-nn`. The backticked `GQ:C-01` to `GQ:C-25` at V1:3107 is a code span and stays as written.
- `R1-Rnn` with nn from 01 to 13 is a run 1 research file (R01 to R13); `R1-Rnn` with nn above 13 is a run 1 debate risk id (for example `R1-R21`). Run 2's R01 to R18 are other files. A bare `R1` to `R9` (no hyphen) inside carried text is an anonymised reviewer id, never a provenance mark.
- Not prefixed: ids inside backticks, URLs and file:line citations; `C3` at V1:169 (a combo run); the probe labels `M1`-`M4` at V1:2704, 2729 and 2761. In 9.11, `R1-Gn` means gap row n and `R1-C1`..`R1-C3` mean closure-effort classes (V1:4126).
- Inside a carried `R1-` block, a bare short label that this rule does not list (for example the V1-V4 `panel verify` checks, T1/T2, the S1-S5 rf-qa sections, the F2/F3 audit rows, the A-1/A-4 audit checks, the K1-K4 MR kernel layers, the B-1..B-4 stages, the M5-M12 probe labels, the P3-B1 QA ids) keeps run 1's meaning and is not a base id.
- Under each carried run 1 legend (V1:108-129, 483-492, 4126) one line says: "In this merged copy, these ids carry the prefix `R1-` (Merge Notes, id rule)".
- Compare ids: three-digit `C-`, `X-`, `S-`, `A-` and `U-` ids in new text (these Merge Notes, lead sentences, notes and Appendices C to F) are ids of the compare's `diff-analysis.md` (for example C-084, X-043). The exception is base text inside V2:3509-3525 and V2:3586-3670, where three-digit ids are points of run 2's own debates. Two-digit `C-01`..`C-15` and `X-13`..`X-15` are run 2's debate slots.
- Invariants found by the compare fault-finder are cited `R25-INV-nnn` (`invariant-probe.md`); they are not the debate-local INV ids of either report.

**Citation form.** In new text (these Merge Notes, lead sentences, notes and Appendices C to F), `V1:<n>` means line n of run 1's report (byte-identical copy `adversarial/variant-1-original.md`) and `V2:<n>` means line n of run 2's report (byte-identical copy `adversarial/variant-2-original.md`); `V2:<n>` refers to the base as it was before the merge, not to this file. Carried blocks keep their own line citations into the repository, which are unchanged.

**(e) E2 evidence pins.** Run 2 reads the E2 branch at `6c0984326cbb8fb06c4a36065de58b171d3f8175`; run 1 read it at `4a22d74213f93837d00c2c314075dd967b9a98e3`, four commits earlier (`git rev-list --count 4a22d74..6c09843` = 4). Commit `e2f2ac268` (2026-11-14 19:19 UTC) is 7 commits after `6c09843` (`git rev-list --count 6c09843..e2f2ac268` = 7); neither report read it, and by owner decision it is folded in later. The E2 files the two reports cite were not changed by those 7 commits (fault-finder notes section 1, row 4; for `audit2.py` and `combos/SPEC.md` re-checked by this merge with `git diff --name-only 6c09843 e2f2ac268`, empty).

**(f) HEAD and line numbers.** The code is identical at `792cf8c52` (run 1's HEAD), `50d4d2b9d` (run 2's HEAD) and `ad8f57560` (HEAD of `ironbelly/shadow-runs` at the merge) for `src`, `tests` and `scripts` (`git diff --stat` empty for both pairs). Line numbers in this document are valid at `ad8f57560`. A later plan must re-check every cited line at the base it cuts its branches from: `origin/master` (`d4d1662a8`) has moved and sits 3 commits past the merge-base `d2d8a2d16` (Baseline and Conventions, merge addendum; R25-INV-001).

**(g) Open items that block a `converged` status.** The 7 HIGH UNADDRESSED invariants of the compare probe are carried as open items, not as settled, in Section 9.12: R25-INV-003 (ledger version skew), R25-INV-006 (read-only mechanism leaves MCP servers available), R25-INV-018 (gate set and gate cross-references), R25-INV-024 (cascade of the clustering trigger T-c), R25-INV-027 (run 1 migration steps that conflict with the adopted design), R25-INV-028 (five outcomes changed or reopened without a new debate) and R25-INV-029 (trigger T-c already met by an agreed fact unless the owner accepts the v1 over-merge). Appendix D lists all 32 probe rows.

**(h) Scope.** This document adds no roadmap, no branch plan, no pull-request plan and no schedule. Run 1's migration steps, gates and risk rows are carried as content; where carried run 1 text uses ordering words, they are run 1's recommendation, not an order of work in this document.

## 1. Problem Statement

- **The question:** Which ONE unified central Review Panel design (a shared core plus thin modules) captures all the value of E1, E2 and E3 and keeps future PR code review and rf-qa replacement unblocked? E1 = reflect Tier 2 panel kernel (merged as `d2d8a2d16` / #519 on 2026-11-12) with its shadow mode and 15-run model-combination experiment; E2 = the tasklist review-panel study, five collaboration designs and two process-redesign brainstorms on `origin/ironbelly/eval-tasklist-review-panel`; E3 = the #346 review loop (`superclaude review` v1 path, spec-panel Review Loop, loop prompts) plus five installed-only variants (R01 header and legend).
- **Why it matters:** The research files establish seven facts that a unified design has to account for.
  - The three efforts overlap in four places only: the finding id regex and findings-v1 grammar, the shared `cli/review` panel engine, the review cap constant 3, and E2's unchanged use of E3's `review merge` (R01 summary, [CODE-VERIFIED]). They conflict in twelve registered places (R01 section 5, C-1 to C-12): finding location type, blocking rule, fingerprint, ledger schema, convergence threshold, exclusion and fallback location, dispatch, report ending, run record, loop-contract vintage.
  - Two Tier 2 engines exist inside E1 and share only `contract.py` (R06 section 8c): the in-process swarm ensemble behind `superclaude reflect run`, and the prose skill panel (`sc-reflect-protocol`) with its shadow engine. The panel kernel in `cli/review` is wired only to the second (R01 section 2, R06 section 4.1).
  - E3i is a second, stdlib-only implementation of the whole loop that imports nothing from `cli/review` and is not installed or removed by `superclaude install` (R01 section 6, R03 section 3.1, R14 section 3, [CODE-VERIFIED]).
  - E2 changed no file under `src/` or `tests/` at any commit (R01 section 1.1, [CODE-VERIFIED]). It contributes data, a working non-Claude dispatch script, collaboration designs and the only ground truth (16 items in 3 packages) (R01, R08).
  - Evidence of quality is thin. E1 has no ground-truth scoring for any of its 30 runs and a Stage 2 exit that reads `OVERALL: FAIL (shadow runs 13 of 20)` (R06 section 6.1, R07 section 3). E2 has 3 packages, one judge and replicates that reuse the same packages (R08 section 7). E1 and E2 are one evidence family: the E1 input is byte-identical to the E2 designSpec candidate, sha256 `044809e3a963fad395cfbe0988bece975650a3adf17176893665d92338bd3481` (R16 Part 6).
  - The defect register holds 171 rows (170 distinct): 75 belong to the core, 29 to the reflect module, 4 to the tasklist and spec modules (R17 final register).
  - Two future consumers depend on specific core properties. The PR code review module needs file:line locations (the findings-v2 parser accepts them, the ledger path does not), module-declared category, lens and severity sets, an optional per-slot lens, and read-only reviewers; rf-qa replacement needs the same set plus a checklist output mode and a behavioural oracle (R13 sections 7-8, [CODE-VERIFIED]). No product code records the served model (R04 section 4.2).
- **Trigger:** Each program reached a committed result by 2026-11-14. E1: kernel #519 (2026-11-12 14:47:10 -0500) plus evidence commits `792cf8c52` and `50d4d2b9d` at HEAD. E2: four commits after the run-1 commit `4a22d7421` (2026-11-13 16:17:36 to 2026-11-14 04:38:11 UTC), including `HANDOFF-review-panel-unification-run2.md`, whose open decision DO4 and question Q7 ask whether tasklist review stays on reflect UC-1 or moves to a unified panel (R11 section 5.1; R01 section 1.1). E3: #478, #479, #482, #484 and #498 on the spec-panel Review Loop, with the phase-5 experiments and the 346Claude plan (R14 section 4). The research files record no decision document that selects a unified design; the unresolved decisions are logged in `gaps-and-questions.md` (555 rows: 243 [UNVERIFIED], 187 OPEN-QUESTION, 67 STALE-DOC, 58 [CODE-CONTRADICTED]).

## 2. Current State Analysis

### 2.1 E1 reflect Tier 2 panel kernel and shadow mode

**What E1 merged.**

| #518 | `167184c6ba449ab49b7f2af1dc9f4c9080006bd3` changes 0 RV files and 1 test file (`tests/review/test_review_panel_live7.py`). E2 run-2 and `HANDOFF-run1-vs-run2.md:22` attribute the RV change to "#519 + #518": [CODE-CONTRADICTED]; the change is #519 alone | R01 s1.3, R17 DR-045 |

**Reflect profile limits on a panel.** A `reflect-*` template is limited to at most 3 reviewers; launch values from the three Claude Code class words only (sonnet, opus, haiku); no Fable model reachable by any slot or stand-in in any environment; every reachable model present in the tier file's `classes` map; a `round_robin` slot needs `--sequence`. The `gateway` environment has `"launch": {}`, so `superclaude review panel resolve --template @reflect-pre --env gateway` fails with `invalid reflect resolution: ... launch None is not one of sonnet, opus, haiku` (reproduced by running the command; `--env anthropic-only` resolves). `review panel validate --kind panel` does not run the profile because it passes no tier file (`panel_cmd.py:124`). The packaged tier file has no `tier0` alias, so the Tier 0 rule at `panel.py:116-117` is inert on packaged data (R04 s2 [CODE-VERIFIED]).

**Two Tier 2 engines that share only `contract.py`.** Provenance: engine A predates the E1 shadow work (master baseline; PRs #213, #214, #220, #329; run 1 V1:414). <!-- Source: Base (original, modified) — M-24 item 12: engine A provenance -->

```
superclaude reflect run --depth standard|deep        (CLI wrapper, headless; the sc-tasklist per-phase terminal gate calls it)
   ReflectRunner._audit_once  (runner.py:538-545)
      |-- Engine A: run_tier2_ensemble (ensemble.py) -> swarm transports, raw T2Model0N ids over HTTP, tasklist text only
      |-- contract.parse_contract + derive_verdict (contract.py:138-260) -> exit 0 / 10 / 11 / 2

/sc:reflect --mode pre|post                           (skill, Claude-orchestrated; reached from sc:workflow Wave 4, tasklist Stage 10.5)
   Engine B: SKILL.md Waves 0-7
      --t2-engine legacy (default): reflect-reviewer agents -> calibrator -> sc-adversarial Mode A -> evidence-validator -> contract 1.8.0
      --t2-engine shadow (UC-1 only): the legacy waves stay authoritative; 10 extra steps call
          superclaude review {panel resolve, manifest init/advance, cluster, verify-citations}; output under <output>/panel/
      --t2-engine panel: rejected ("ships in Stage 3")

Shared between A and B: contract.parse_contract / derive_verdict only (B reaches them offline through scripts/reflect_verdict_replay.py).
Panel kernel (cli/review): used by B's shadow steps only; Grep finds no import of superclaude.cli.review in cli/reflect.

**Verdict map and contract (what any Tier 2 engine must feed).** `derive_verdict` is a pure function with order blocked, degraded, halted, pass (`contract.py:138-260`). It reads 19 contract fields; it ignores unknown keys; it accepts any major version `1`. It never reads `merged-verdict.yaml`, `reviewer_cards` or `evidence_validator_ran`. 36 tests in `tests/cli/reflect/test_verdict_mapping.py` pin it (exit 0 pass, 10 halted, 11 degraded, 2 blocked). The 1.8.0 field lists are 110 stable names and 27 telemetry names in `panel_lint.py:33-174`, tied to SKILL.md sections 9.1 and 9.2 by `test_pinned_field_lists_match_skill_md`; the "byte-identical" tests compare with `HEAD`, so they bind uncommitted edits only. `panel_lint` is called only from `scripts/reflect_shadow_exit.py` and tests (R06 s1, s3, s5.6 [CODE-VERIFIED]).

Six points where the skill text and the code disagree, none reconciled by a test (R06 s5.4, [CODE-VERIFIED] on both sides):

| Point | SKILL.md | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Convergence threshold | `>=0.75 PASS, >=0.60 PARTIAL, <0.60 FAIL` (`SKILL.md:703`) | `contract.py:317-326` degrades a present score below `0.80`; tests pin both sides of 0.80 (`test_verdict_mapping.py:432-458`); tasklist T5 also uses 0.80 (R11 s2.3) |
| `t2_model_class_diversity` values | `full \| degraded` | engine A emits `full \| insufficient`; `contract.py:283` degrades on any non-`full` |
| Single vendor | "warn-only in v1.0" (`SKILL.md:839`) | `contract.py:287-288` DEGRADES (exit 11) unless `--allow-single-vendor` |
| `contract_version` | `1.8.0` | engine A emits `1.0` (`ensemble.py:74, 788`); `panel_lint.py:185` demands `1.8.0` |
| `merge_method` meaning | set only after a real merge | set by count in engine A |
| Contract growth rule | additive fields are a MINOR bump, consumers read-and-ignore (`SKILL.md:1019-1021`) | `panel_lint.py:360-365` treats any new top-level key as needing a bump the Stage 2 plan "does not make" |

Further verified facts: `reviewer_briefs_materialized` is instructed by `refs/reviewer-spec.md:51, 57, 78` but is in neither the 110-name nor the 27-name list nor SKILL.md 9.1/9.2, so a run that follows the ref fails lint rule L2 (5 of 15 combo runs) (R06 s3.3). `--fix` is passed by the tasklist gate but the swarm contract carries no `remediation_*` pointer. The CLI default is `--promote` (`commands.py:236-239`) while a runner comment says `--no-promote` is the hard default (`runner.py:457`) (R06 s4.2).

**What the wrapper (engine A's shell) provides, independent of which engine supplies reviewers (R06 s4, [CODE-VERIFIED]).** Code-enforced four-state exit codes with fail-closed gating; atomic frontmatter write-back; a recursion marker (`SUPERCLAUDE_REFLECT_WRAPPER_ACTIVE`, R11 s2.3); a reviewer-isolation snapshot (`create_review_snapshot`, `config.py:155-210`, "PINNED OFF" by default at `models.py:94`); a bounded Tier-1 fallback ladder (`fallback.py`: `FALLBACK_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES = {timeout, proxy_error, parse_error}`, 8 terminal reasons, a `QuorumState` of at least 2 reviewers, at least 2 distinct model ids and not single-vendor); and a credit-free stub transport. `--reviewers` is clamped to [2,4] with 1 kept as a negative witness (`config.py:334-335`); the wrapper resolves no panel template, persona or tier file (its model choice is the `T2Model0N` / `T1Model0N` slots, a third registry besides the skill's `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` and the tier JSON).

**What is held byte-identical today (R06 s8a, [CODE-VERIFIED]).** (1) The consumer-read 1.8.0 field names: the SKILL.md 9.3 consumer map names fields by value for sc-troubleshoot, `superclaude sprint run`, sc-task, sc:roadmap, sc:tasklist, sc-workflow, task-builder, Wave 7 and CI, and states that removal or rename needs a major bump (`SKILL.md:1011, 1021`); additions are minor and consumers must read-and-ignore (`:1020, 1038`). (2) The `merge_method` values `{adversarial, single-reviewer-fallback}` (`panel_lint.LEGAL_MERGE_METHODS`, `contract.py:295`). (3) The verdict map and its 36 tests. (4) The four deviation keys `authorized, necessary, drift, regression` (`contract.py:40`, `classify_fix`, Wave 7 condition 4 at `SKILL.md:1540`). (5) The reviewer brief structure (exactly three sections, `test_shadow_skill_contract.py:146`) and the findings-block grammar. (6) The artifact layout read by EV-1 (`adversarial/merged-verdict.yaml`, `reviewer-cards/reviewer-<N>-card.*`, an `audit.log` row matching `F2|F3`). Not inherently byte-identical: the literal `1.8.0` and the "no new key" rule are a Stage 2 convention with a documented minor-bump path (adding `reviewer_briefs_materialized` would need SKILL.md 9.1, both lint constants, `test_f3_f4_contract_version`, and the wording at `panel_lint.py:363-365`, and no consumer change by the 9.4 rule); the byte-identity tests compare with the current `HEAD`, so they freeze nothing across commits. ### 2.2 E2 tasklist review-panel study and its evidence

**What E2 is in the repository.** E2 is the branch `origin/ironbelly/eval-tasklist-review-panel` (tip `6c0984326cbb8fb06c4a36065de58b171d3f8175`, 4 commits after the run-1 commit `4a22d7421`: `c2ddeb1b4` 2026-11-13 16:17:36 UTC, `fd69a006d` 20:25:07, `d561461fa` 2026-11-14 04:37:57, `6c0984326` 04:38:11). `git diff --stat` from `4a22d7421` to the tip and from the merge-base `ec259f1b7` to the tip, restricted to `src` and `tests`, print nothing, and each of the four commits changes 0 files there. E2 is evidence, harness scripts, design documents and out-of-tree prototype code under `.dev/eval-workspaces/`; it adds no product module (R01 s1.1, [CODE-VERIFIED]). Its manifest line "local, never pushed" is stale: the branch is on origin (R01, R16).

E2 session tooling writes into E1's evidence tree: `snap.py:4` opens `.../shadow-model-combos/runs/pre-TASK-WF-designSpec-20261107-075614-comboD-r1/artifacts/input-snapshot.yaml` for writing, and `rlog-r3.sh:3` appends to the comboE-r3 `audit.log`; `drift-b3.py:2` only reads. A read-only recomputation of the script's hash formula gives `17ff5b8a9589047325faa3eb2755996d61f4a54fe77a0336166ecbaf42cec4e9`, identical to the value in E1's committed file. Exactly three files at the tip reference `brainstorm-reflect-panel`. That the E2 script rather than another process wrote the E1 file is an inference from format and hash identity (R01 s1.2).

**The harness (`.dev/eval-workspaces/tasklist-review-panel/20261111-a1/tools/`).** [CODE-VERIFIED by `git show` at the tip, R04 s3.4, R05 unit 3, R16 part 1]

| Component | Verified behaviour | Defect found |
|---|---|---|
| `run-reviewer.sh` (87 lines) | one reviewer per call: `claude -p --model "$MODEL" --output-format json --no-session-persistence --permission-mode bypassPermissions --disallowedTools Edit Write NotebookEdit` run from `/tmp/evalsb/repo`, `timeout 3000`, 2 attempts per model, then a hand-kept fallback ladder (`:23-43, :66-83`) | Bash is not disallowed; `/tmp/evalsb` and the `source.md` origin are absolute harness constants |
| Brief (`:13-17`) | `/sc:spec-panel @<candidate> --mode critique` plus the first-review brief of the loop; states anchor 12 to 200 characters and the six categories; does not state the 300-character claim cap; never names `source.md` | `source.md` is copied beside the candidate (`:9-11`) and every failure path ends in `|| true`, so a missing source is silent |
| Identity check (`:51-58, :76`) | `MODEL_OK` compares the unique top-level `assistant` `message.model` with `$MODEL` and writes `meta.json` | `MODEL="$NEXT"` overwrites `$MODEL` before the next attempt, so after a fallback `expected_model` is the fallback model and a silent swap passes |
| `BLOCK_OK` (`:57`) | true when a line starts with the `findings-v1` fence | a fence of invalid lines passes |
| `judge-one.sh` | `claude -p --model claude-opus-5-5 --permission-mode bypassPermissions`; the judge writes `score.json` itself; OK means exit code 0 and `judge.json` parses as JSON; skipped if `score.json` exists | no check that `score.json` exists, parses or matches the schema; a judge that died after writing a plausible file is never re-run (this produced the retracted `n2-sonnet-src` "8/14") |
| `anon-combos.sh` | replaces reviewer ids with `R<i>`, strips the eval path, random labels Q..V | model identity inside claim text and `.catfix` file names is not hidden; judge isolation is a prose rule while `bypassPermissions` is on |
| Judge prompt | counts a GT item as "blocking" when a blocking ledger row covers it | ignores the GT item's own `blocking_in_implement`, so judge-blocking differs from real blocking |

**Ground truth.** `ground-truth.json` in three packages: designSpec 10 items (GT1-GT5 `blocking_in_implement` true), makeTheAliasOnly 4 items (GT1-GT3 true, GT4 false; GT5 and GT6 in `dropped` with reasons), control `design` 2 items (none blocking). Each item carries `quote_grep_count` (1 for all 16) and `evidence_ok`. GT classes (`unpassable-ac`, `ambiguity`, `contradiction`, `missing-task`) are a different vocabulary from the findings categories. Evidence comes from one implement run per plan (`progress.md`, `review-N.md`, ...), so a true novel defect scores as a wrong blocker. sha256 of the three files: designSpec `3e56551dc0046c9f...cb47e4`, alias `79e3205775deace4...f5eb1e`, design `e3585b8e6bf11241...975a3c` (R16 s3.1, [CODE-VERIFIED]). **What the study does not show (R08 s7, [CODE-VERIFIED] or recomputed).** No product-panel result: every run used raw model ids through `run-reviewer.sh`, not `superclaude review panel` dispatch. Ground truth is 16 defects in 3 packages, 4 of which were never caught and 3 of which carry about 89-91% of catches. No gate-accuracy measurement and no multi-round evidence: every ledger is round 1 only. One Opus judge pass per (row, package). No audited-clean evidence for the final recommendation. Tokens are reviewer OUTPUT tokens only (no dollar cost, no input tokens), and `elapsed` assumes full parallelism. Reviewer and judge sessions cannot be re-run from the commit: `git ls-tree -r` finds 0 `judge.json` and 0 `attempt*.json`; 2,916 files (1.48 GB) were left on the original machine (`RAW-TRANSCRIPTS-NOT-COMMITTED.md:2`). The proposed harness fixes (raise the anchor limit, name `source.md` in the brief) are implemented nowhere in `src`; batch j1 shows luna still refuses when a nested input is missing.

**Reproducibility of the analysis scripts.** `final-table.py` run with its 5 hard-coded environment paths patched reproduces the committed header (`valid-era rows: 71; row-packages scored: 213; ... carrying an audit EXCLUDE flag: 69`) and a byte-identical `final-table.md`. Defect: `fullpkg()` (`final-table.py:15-18`) matches ids by a 12-character prefix, and the control package id `TASK-WF-design-20261108-041415` returns the designSpec id (both begin `TASK-WF-desi`). Effect: 59 EXCLUDE flags naming the control package are applied to designSpec and 11 flags with truncated or `*` package names exclude all three packages; the corrected exclusion count is 71 (29 / 24 / 18) or 76 (31 / 25 / 20), not 69 (41 / 25 / 3). The AS-SCORED table is unaffected (it skips the exclusion test); the AUDIT-CLEAN table (`COMBO-REPORT.md:339-359`) is mis-computed, `COMBO-REPORT.md:361` already calls it a robustness view only, R08 reports the conclusion direction unchanged, and the corrected clean table was not recomputed ([UNVERIFIED], GQ-099). `three-way.py:19` prints `p[:8]` = `TASK-WF-` as the flagged package, so that column is unreadable. Of audits A to F only A and D have written summaries; the audit-A summary disagrees with its own `flags.tsv` (59 against 54 for check E2, 9 against 1 for E11, "930" against "890" runs) (R08 s4, R16 s2, [CODE-VERIFIED]).

**E1 and E2 are one evidence family (R16 part 6, [CODE-VERIFIED]).** The E1 input tasklist is byte-identical to the E2 designSpec `candidate.md` (sha256 `044809e3a963fad395cfbe0988bece975650a3adf17176893665d92338bd3481`; the same bytes sit in E1 `input/` and in `.dev/tasks/done/`); E1 chose the package because it has the most ground truth; E1 chose combinations C and E from E2's results (`PLAN.md:96-105`); E1's optional quality scoring reads E2's ground truth from commit `b4db265a8` (an ancestor of the E2 tip, not of HEAD); both run on the same kernel code (`findings.py` and `ledger.py` unchanged since the E2 base); both ran on the same gateway on adjacent days. ### 2.3 E2 collaboration designs and process-redesign brainstorms

Both are design-and-prototype work on the E2 branch. Neither adds product code (R01 s1.1); neither has a measured effect on the 14 known defects (R09 s2.3, [CODE-VERIFIED]).

**A. Parallel-collaboration designs (brainstorm `20261113-163248-panel-collaboration`, packages r1 to r5 under `.dev/eval-workspaces/tasklist-review-panel/20261113-collab/`).**

Slate and mechanism (R09 s1, [CODE-VERIFIED] from the E2 tip):

| Package | Family | Content exchanged | Author | Delivery |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| r1 Move Radar | F3 content-free coverage steering | one catalogue move (at most 300 characters) or a "source.md not opened" check | harness (jq classifier on the reviewer's telemetry) | PostToolUse hook, JSON `additionalContext`, at tool-call checkpoints |
| r2 Idle-Shift Sweeper | F4 searcher-to-reader fact relay | repo facts (paths, counts, `path:line`, the command) | a helper ember session through a Bash helper `panel-post` | PostToolUse hook on two luna receivers, one fact per call from call 6 |
| r3 Axis-Flip Challenge | F1 between-phase cross-examination | a peer anchor or a random "gap card" plus one move, in a digest | harness from sealed phase-1 findings | between-phase `claude -p --resume <session_id>` second pass |
| r4 Flag-and-Adjudicate | F7 directed challenge | a card (anchor plus move) | the flagger model through `panel-post` | PostToolUse hook on two luna adjudicators after call 6 |
| r5 Coverage Deflection | F6 steering a running strong model | Task ids not covered by any finished scout (`kind: "coverage"`) | harness watcher | PostToolUse hook on the receiver |

Arms: A0 today's harness; A1 = A0 plus the harness fixes H1-H4; A2 = A1 plus a static move kit M1-M10 in every brief, no communication; A3 F1, A4 F4, A5 F7, A6 F3; Stage 2 A1-SL2, A2-SL2, F6-SL2 (R09 s1.1). F2 and F5 were evicted from the slate by a distinctness rule; the 25-proposal family table was not opened ([UNVERIFIED]).

The four hook-based packages implement one skeleton four times: parameters baked into the command string; always exit 0 and fail open; subagent calls (`agent_id` set) logged and never counted or delivered; per-reviewer call counter under `flock`; a finish signal once at `FINISH_MS`; no delivery before the 6th main call; seal = copy `transcript_path` plus sha256 immediately before first delivery, fail closed; output exactly `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PostToolUse","additionalContext":...}}`. Differences: r1 seals at the checkpoint even when no item is then chosen, r2, r4 and r5 seal only when a delivery is about to happen; r4 adds a forgery check. Only F4 and F7 need a model that can write (Bash helper); F1, F3, F6 are harness-authored (R09 s1.2-1.3, [CODE-VERIFIED]).

Evidence status of the designs ([CODE-VERIFIED] unless marked):

| Item | Verified fact |
|---|---|
| Missing code | `git ls-tree -r` of each package shows 0 paths containing `/lib/` (file counts r1 107, r2 321, r3 130, r4 70, r5 274). The root `.gitignore:13` is `lib/` and `:79` is `*.log`. Tracked scripts that source the missing files: r2 `bin/launch-panel.sh:6`, `bin/hooks/receiver-hook.sh:10, 85`; r3 `bin/launch-panel.sh:5, 55`; r4 `bin/r4-hook:10`. r2, r3 and r4 (and, per its own IMPLEMENTATION.md, r5) cannot run from the commit; r1 keeps its tools but `values/` and `runs/` are untracked |
| Test counts, claimed against static `def test_` counts at the tip | r1 138 / 103; r2 358 / 163; r3 89 / 89; r4 106 / 90; r5 108 / 82. Only r3 matches; pytest was not run. r5 `tests/last-run.txt` records `108 passed` as a log |
| Measured rows | single smoke rows on the 2-item control package. r1 `gate0.json`: S3 and Spike 4 missing; r2 `spikes/RESULTS.md`: S3 FAIL three times then "PASS" as a re-grading after an audit-rule fix; r3 `smoke.jsonl` 4 rows (A3 158.8 s twice, A1 95.2 and 154.8 s, `phase2_timeout` 1 in both A3 rows); r4 `act-rates.json` (haiku 0/0, sonnet 0.6/1, luna 0/0.4, ember 0/0); r5 `results.jsonl` 5 rows |
| Only weighty number | r5: the static kit alone on sonnet cost +59% elapsed (281.6 s against a 176.9 s A1 mean) and +55% output tokens (46,018 against 29,655), one package, three runs |
| Hook latency | measured p95 73 and 81 ms (r2), 57-85 ms (r5), against a 0.1 s design budget; r4's 143 and 90 ms are slice-sourced ([UNVERIFIED]) |
| Defect-package results | none. `found_14` is null or 0 everywhere; the design text itself says the plan cannot detect the central gain at n=12 (`merged-requirements.md:1128`) |

What the runtimes at HEAD can host (R09 s4.2, [CODE-VERIFIED]): `reflect-reviewer` has the tool allowlist Read, Grep, Glob, augment search, auggie retrieval and codegraph (no Bash, Edit, Write or Task), `model: sonnet`, `maxTurns: 50`, `permissionMode: plan`, no `hooks:` key, and is told "you do not coordinate with the other reviewers". It can be a receiver of harness-authored items but never a sweeper or flagger (no Bash for `panel-post`). The E2 hook scripts skip any call that carries `agent_id`, so a reviewer that is itself a subagent receives nothing from them; whether PostToolUse `additionalContext` reaches a subagent's own model is [UNVERIFIED] (the E2 spikes show delivery only for main-thread `claude -p` sessions). Engine A's swarm worker sends one user message and reads text back (`openai_compat.py:384-388`): no tool loop, no hook point, no session to resume. `reflect --resume` at HEAD (`commands.py:290-294, 552-553`) means "skip the launch when the prior reflect_post passed on HEAD", not a model-session resume. Between-phase exchange (F1) is the only family that needs neither a hook nor a model-side write, but it has no clean measured success in any runtime and its `--resume` dependency for gateway ids is [UNVERIFIED].

Harness fixes H1-H4 in the source documents are harness fixes, not transport requirements (`merged-requirements.md:311-318`): H1 name the driving document in the brief; H2 truncate anchor and claim, validate with the real parser, re-ask once; H3 sandbox from the commit the plan was written against; H4 remove leak directories. At HEAD `findings.py:104, 118` and `findings_v2.py:111, 126, 132, 136` still reject an anchor over 200 and a claim over 300 characters. H3's base rule differs by package (r4 `manifest.json` has empty `first_commit`; r5 `sandbox-build.sh:25` runs `git add -A` without `-f`, losing tracked-but-ignored files). The transport rules (R-21, R-22, seal, board) apply only while an exchange arm is on (R09 s5).

Conflict log of the designs: 36 logged conflicts (X1-X17 between r1 and r2, C-01 to C-19 across r3-r5) classified by R09 as 13 decidable by evidence in hand, 4 partly, 4 not decidable now (X1, X2, C-06, C-14: act-rate probes disagree, for luna from 0 to 0.8 across r1, r2, r4, r5), 15 design decisions. Examples verified at file:line: X8 seal timing (r1 `radar-hook.sh:53-65` seals before choosing an item, r2 `receiver-hook.sh:69-83` seals immediately before the first delivery, matching requirement text at `merged-requirements.md:232`); C-11 (r5 `git add -A` without `-f`); C-15 (hook latency).

E2's own statement (`merged-requirements.md:917`): "The static kit (A2) may beat every exchange design on gross gain ... If none does, the right design is the cheapest one: the harness fixes plus the kit in the brief." No measurement compares any exchange arm with A2 (R09 s7).

**panel-msg/1 and the `origin` key (R02 s8, [CODE-VERIFIED]).** `panel-msg/1` is a transport message (keys `v, id, run, from, to, t, kind, move, anchor, items, n`; at most 600 BYTES; unknown keys rejected; forbidden keys `claim, verdict, blocking, severity, category, note`). `origin` (`own` | `peer`) is a key of the findings line, not of `panel-msg/1`. Both `findings.py` and `findings_v2.py` accept it (and any unknown key except v2's `calibrated_confidence`), so the in-line placement works at HEAD; the merge keeps the line whole but the ledger member record stores only `round, reviewer_id, fid, blocking` (`ledger.py:172-202`), so the tag is lost at merge. Nothing under `src/superclaude/cli/review/` reads `origin`. The name `origin` already means other things in two E3i variants (`review_ledger.py`: `find` / `changed` / `outside` / `sweep`; `diffgate.py:729-733`: `full` / `changed` / `unchanged`) (see 2.4 and 2.5).

**B. Process-redesign brainstorms (`.dev/brainstorms/20261113-223124-panel-process-redesign/`, requirements file `merged-requirements.md`, 1254 lines at the tip).** (R10, [GIT-VERIFIED] / [CODE-VERIFIED])

| Element | Verified content |
|---|---|
| Two redesigns | Sweep Sheet (a deterministic script builds up to 12 items from extractors E1-E7, assigns 24 slots = 12 items x 2 of 3 blind reviewers; MR2:376-409) and Recipe Ledger (no pre-pass; each reviewer carries a lens of 2-4 class recipes bound to MODEL NAMES; MR2:678-759) |
| Class table | 8 classes C1-C8 induced from ten missed issues and an E2 recurrence search; strength column: C2, C4, C5, C6, C8 "General", C1 "symptom-level only", C3 "Weak" (MR2:99-110). The same ten issues map to the collaboration brainstorm's moves M1-M10 (each move lands in exactly one class), so class cards subsume the move catalogue |
| Carrier and checks | a per-reviewer `ledger-v1` fenced block (`item, verdict OK|PROBLEM|UNSURE, quote_plan, quote_other, problem, ran`); post-run substring checks that demote an unsupported PROBLEM row's linked finding and promote an unlinked PROBLEM row to a MINOR finding tagged `src=ledger` (MR2:266-319) |
| Gates | G0 offline and D1-D7 (time at most 1.35 x Z0; D2 effect at least Z0 + 0.12 absolute with a 90% bootstrap lower bound above Z0 + 0.04; ...). D2's 0.12 on a 14-item scale is 1.68 items, against central planning shares of +1.33 and +1.05 items (0.095 and 0.075), so the gate is stricter than the design's own central case (inputs are planning values) |
| Status | design only: `grep` for `PROBLEM`, `UNSURE`, `quote_plan`, `ledger-v1`, `Sweep Sheet`, `Recipe Ledger` over `src/superclaude/cli` returns 0 matches; MR2:24 says all probabilities, factors and time figures are planning values |

What E1 already has that the redesign duplicates (R10 unit 6): the `{reviewer: {assigned, observed}}` sidecar (`SKILL.md:345`, `cluster_cmd.py:113-117`, `verify_cmd.py:99-105`, validated by `findings_v2.coverage_context` and `check_finding` at `:166-176`; an empty block is valid only if every assigned row is observed, `:291-298`); one quote normaliser (`verify_cmd._norm` and `findings.flat` are both `" ".join(text.split())`); an advisory citation precheck (`verify_cmd._check`: `missing-file`, `out-of-range`, `quote-not-found`; "drops nothing", `verify_cmd.py:11-12`); a requirement-row producer in prose for UC-1 (`SKILL.md:278`, `refs/coverage-mapping.md:50-60`, which overlaps E2's extractor E5 for class C2). What E1 does not have: producers for classes C1, C3-C8, a per-row verdict, a quote pair per row, and demote or promote of findings. E2's promotion writes a finding the reviewer did not write, whereas E1's checks are advisory and "the validator alone decides drops".

Recorded E1 data for that flow (R10 unit 10, [CODE-VERIFIED]): 13 `coverage.json` sidecars (row ids are free-form strings chosen by the orchestrator, one has a range token, 11 of 13 have a row assigned to more than one reviewer or twice, 2 of 13 have `observed` empty for every reviewer); 29 `precheck.json` files: 1,047 citations checked, 510 flagged (48.7%), by reason 472 `not-in-snapshot` (92.5% of flags), 7 `out-of-range`, 31 `quote-not-found` (3.0% of all citations); card block states over the same 29 runs 77 complete and 10 invalid (11.5%). In recorded data the precheck mostly flags paths outside the snapshot, not wrong quotes.

Decidability of the redesign's items at HEAD (R10 unit 7): a mechanical test is possible for C4 (run the literal criterion command) and C8 (`git grep -l` of each edited path over tests, scripts, docs); candidate lists only for C2 and C5; C1, C3, C7 and X3-X6 need judgment; X7 is weak by E2's own note. Ten `.dev/reflect/**/REPORT.md` instance cites re-read at HEAD exist and show a defect of the stated shape (one classification doubt: C6 or C5). Every gate G0 and D1-D7 is a numeric design choice that no recorded run can evaluate because no arm, extractor, hold-out ground truth or planted set exists.

Seed-brief claims checked against code (R10 unit 8): "grades a requirement the plan never states as Medium (non-blocking)" holds (`document_review_loop_prompts.md:31-32`; Medium is a grade outside the severity enum); "has no missing-task category" is [CODE-CONTRADICTED] in part (`CATEGORIES` has `missing-requirement`, `findings.py:15-22`; no category is named `missing-task`); "defines no severity levels" is [CODE-CONTRADICTED] (`SEVERITIES = (CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR)`, `findings.py:14`; the brief gives no definition separating CRITICAL from MAJOR, and severity does not change the verdict, which depends on `blocking` and status); "does not name any driving document" holds (placeholders `{{CANDIDATE}}`, `{{BASELINE}}`, `{{PRIOR}}`, `{{N}}`, `{{IDS}}` only).

**Policy conflict between the programs.** E2 requirement R-02 truncates `anchor` and `anchor2` to 200 and `claim` to 300 as an exact prefix, then re-asks once for what is still invalid; E1's protocol says the orchestrator "never edits, remaps or normalizes a reviewer's findings itself" and allows one bounded re-ask for an invalid block (`SKILL.md:343`). Both give one re-ask; only E2 truncates (R02 s5.3 key takeaway, [CODE-VERIFIED] as text of both documents; neither runs in `cli/review`).

**Corrections ([CODE-CONTRADICTED]).** `r1 DESIGN.md:7` ("Nothing here is implemented yet") and `r2 DESIGN.md:5` ("design only") are stale: both packages contain built tools and an IMPLEMENTATION.md. `r2 IMPLEMENTATION.md` lists `bin/lib/*` as built, but the commit has no `lib/` path. The statement that between-phase exchange "works in every runtime" was withdrawn in R09 fix cycle 1. The slice-07 reading that r1 and r2 luna act rates are "compatible" is weakened by r4 and r5 (0/5 and 1/5). `findings_v2.py:3-4` (docstring) is accurate: the one rejected extra key is `calibrated_confidence`; an earlier R10 text that called it stale was retracted in fix cycle 1.

**Contradictions between research files.** R09 s5 calls H2 (truncate before merge) "UNCONDITIONAL, belongs in the core"; R02 s5.3 shows that E1's protocol forbids orchestrator-side normalisation and that v2 clustering turns one bad line into a lost reviewer, so where the repair sits is open (GQ-021). No factual contradiction between R09 and R10.

**Not verified (for Section 9).** All collaboration estimates (reach, act rates, hook cost, +29% kit estimate) and the claimed test counts (GQ-110); the unreadable r2-r5 engines (GQ-111); r3 and r4 result rows and r4 hook p95 (GQ-113); whether `additionalContext` reaches a subagent (GQ-114); which common act-rate probe to use (GQ-117); the value of any exchange capability before an arm beats the static kit (GQ-118); the debate and diff-analysis artifacts of the brainstorm (GQ-119); MR2 sections and the 46 requirements not re-read at source (GQ-125); recurrence counts as phrase-search lower bounds (GQ-126); whether any of the 12 Python files matching the Wave 1B terms implements E1's matcher (GQ-127); the rename of the row block (GQ-129); demote/promote rights (GQ-130); where lens-to-reviewer binding lives given closed slot keys (GQ-131).

- They share no code and no vocabulary with `cli/review`: all four scripts import only the standard library and contain zero references to `superclaude`, `cli.review` or `review panel`; no `findings-v1`, `fixmap-v1`, `review-ledger/1` or `resolved_check` string appears in the four skill folders or the five commands.

ARM B is the 472-line PR 427 text with a renamed `name:` line (sha256 prefix `c8d80346a96cb528`).
- None of them is a multi-reviewer merge; each is a single-reviewer loop (R03 s3.2).

### 2.5 The review package: v1 and v2 pipelines and their shared code

**Layout (R18 s9, [CODE-VERIFIED]).** `src/superclaude/cli/review/` holds 25 tracked files: 16 Python modules (5,086 lines: `__init__` 36, `card_convert` 517, `cluster` 487, `cluster_cmd` 197, `findings` 457, `findings_v2` 304, `ledger` 494, `ledger_cmd` 137, `manifest` 534, `manifest_cmd` 240, `merge_cmd` 118, `panel` 707, `panel_cmd` 129, `telemetry` 447, `telemetry_cmd` 98, `verify_cmd` 184) and nine JSON files under `data/` (`review-tiers.default.json` and eight `review-panel.*.json` templates). `__init__.py:14-36` defines the click group `review` and loads subcommand modules by name, skipping a missing module; `lint_cmd` and `estimate_cmd` are registered but no such files exist. `cli/main.py:568-570` registers `superclaude review`. The package is independent of `cli/reflect`. Tests live in `tests/review/` (19 test files plus fixtures). A `/sc:review` command or `sc-review-protocol` skill does not exist.

**The two pipelines and the code they share.**

```
v1 (E3s, spec loop and E2's study)                         v2 (E1 shadow mode, reflect lenses)
reviewer report: ## Findings block, ```findings-v1          reviewer card (*.md): header lines persona / model_class / model,
        |                                                         ## Findings block, ```findings-v2, then ```yaml calibration:
findings.parse_block  (anchor 12-200 REQUIRED)               findings_v2.parse_block (anchor OR citations, lens, deviation_class, ...)
        |                                                         |
ledger.merge_round: annotate -> locate(anchor), first          cluster_v2: citation role/path/line spans (tolerance 3), chain flag
  occurrence; union-find cluster (3-line tolerance);               verify-citations: review-precheck/1 (advisory, drops nothing)
  match first existing row; blocking = any; severity max          manifest: review-panel-manifest/1 (state machine, per-attempt records)
        |                                                         |
ledger revise / defer / verdict / capture                       panel/clusters.json, precheck.json, coverage.json, manifest.json
  (review-ledger/1, cap 3, exit 0 / 10 / 11)                       (shadow only; never changes a verdict)

shared by both: findings.py  _ID, CATEGORIES, SEVERITIES, _blocks_after, _check_flat, _HEAD_FINDINGS (imported by findings_v2.py:15-22)
                findings.refs_norm / _REF_TOKEN (cluster.annotate calls it, cluster.py:64,141); telemetry._ID_TOKEN is a second copy of the regex
                panel.py + data/*.json (tier resolution) for both; telemetry.py (no automatic writer)
v1 and v2 cannot flow through each other's downstream code (probes P-a, P-b below).
```

Conflicts registered in R01 s5 (all [CODE-VERIFIED] except C-5 statuses and C-11): C-1 v1 accepts `calibrated_confidence` and `prior` lines, v2 rejects both (probe P-b); C-2 blocking rule (E3 allows MAJOR non-blocking; v2 with `reflect_category` forces `blocking == (severity != MINOR)`, `findings_v2.py:161-162`); C-3 location type (quoted anchor against file:line citations; probe P-a); C-4 fingerprint (v1 `sha256("v1|section|refs")[:16]`, v2 `sha256("v2|role|path||refs|class")` full hex); C-5 two ledgers; C-6 convergence 0.75 against 0.80; C-7 exclusion and fallback in a script against tier data; C-8 dispatch; C-9 report ending and brief shape; C-10 run record; C-11 loop-contract vintage (variants); C-12 the cap constant 3, identical everywhere.

**The finding contract (R02, [CODE-VERIFIED] by reading and execution).**

| Rule | v1 `findings.py` | v2 `findings_v2.py` |
|---|---|---|
| Container | heading `## Findings block` (any level, case-insensitive), one fenced block, info string `findings-v1` | same container, info string `findings-v2` |
| Location | `anchor` 12..200 characters (after whitespace flattening) REQUIRED; optional `anchor2` 12..200 | `anchor` OR `citations[]` (1..8 of `{role, path, line_start, line_end, quote?}`; role in plan, spec, source, test, diff, artifact; repo-relative path; quote 12..200) |
| Other limits | claim at most 300; refs at most 8; id `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,15}$`; MINOR cannot be blocking | the same numbers, restated as literals (`:80, 111, 114-120, 126, 128, 132, 136`) through the imported `_check_flat` mechanism |
| Vocabularies | 3 severities, 6 categories (contradiction, unpassable-check, data-loss, safety, missing-requirement, other) | the same, plus lenses `spec` / `reflect-pre` / `reflect-post`, `channel`, `deviation_class` (required when the lens is `reflect-post`), `reflect_category` (ordering, acceptance, coverage, contradiction, risk, deviation), `coverage_rows`, `self_confidence` |
| Unknown keys | accepted and carried | accepted, except `calibrated_confidence` (rejected, `:96-97`); `origin`, `bogus` and `probe` pass |
| `prior` lines | accepted (resolved / open / regressed) | not handled |
| Cost of a bad line | the line is dropped, the reviewer's other lines are kept in the ledger (`ledger.py:135-138`), the merge is refused only if NO reviewer block is valid (`:150-157`) | the line is dropped and the block becomes `invalid`; `cluster._members` skips the whole reviewer (`cluster.py:256-257`); `verify-citations` still verifies the invalid block's findings (`verify_cmd.py:133-140`) |

Probes executed at HEAD (R01 s3, R02 s3-4, [CODE-VERIFIED by execution]): P-a `annotate()` on a citations-only finding raises `KeyError: 'anchor'` (`findings.py:349`), and `ledger.merge_round` calls `annotate` (`ledger.py:136`); mechanism refinement from Gate 1: `merge_round` parses with the v1 `parse_block`, which already requires `anchor`, so a v2 block does not reach `annotate` through that path, and the KeyError arises when a v2-validated citations-only finding is passed to `annotate` directly. P-b a line with `calibrated_confidence` is valid in v1 and invalid in v2. P-c anchor 201, claim 301 and quote 201 characters are each rejected in v2 as in v1. P-d `refs_norm({'anchor':'Task T01.02 does x','claim':'T01.02 bad','refs':['T01.02','AC-0.4','1.2']})` returns `['1.2', 'AC-0.4']`: `T01.01`-style task ids are legal finding ids but are not refs; `_REF_TOKEN` (`findings.py:29`) needs 1-4 capital letters, a hyphen and digits, or `P<digit>`; `telemetry._ID_TOKEN` (`:23`) is a second copy, without the `SHA-` filter. Effect: findings are kept, refs ignored, clustering falls back to proximity; v2 clustering inherits it (`cluster.py:64, 141`). The v2 fingerprint hashes role, path, an empty section and refs, never line numbers, so two findings with the same primary path and the same extractable ref cluster at ANY distance (executed). Anchor-only findings never cluster in v2 (singleton clusters).

**What a dropped line costs (R02 s5, units re-derived).** The 92 / 80 / 49 of the E2 study are finding lines, reviewer-merges and blocking finding lines. Of the 92 lines, 88 (56 + 18 + 14) are length failures that truncation would address, 4 are not (3 bad severity, 1 bad refs; 1 of them blocking); of the 49 blocking lines 48 are length failures. Recovery by re-ask is unmeasured (E2 Spike 5 was not run); keep-and-warn recovers 0. A v2 card that holds one over-length anchor loses the whole reviewer in clustering, whereas the v1 ledger loses one finding. The loss unit therefore depends on which pipeline a finding enters. `card_convert.py` is the only place that truncates (claims to 297 characters plus `...`; `refs` always `[]`; never a quote). Neither brief states every limit: the v1 brief states the 12-200 anchor only (`prompts:60`); the reflect brief (`reviewer-spec.md:39`) states claim and citation limits but not the quote length.

**Merge, ledger and verdict behaviour (R03, [CODE-VERIFIED by read-only execution at HEAD; numbering "D-n" is the review-package defect list of scope slice 09, not the run-2 hand-off's "Dn"]).**

| Behaviour | Reproduced result |
|---|---|
| Clearing by absence (D-1), `ledger.py:254-258` | a row found by 3 of 3 round-1 reviewers is `resolved` and the round is PASS because ONE other reviewer returned an empty block in round 2; `merge_round` does not check that `doc_text` is the text `apply_revision` produced; the docstring at `ledger.py:112` ("an invalid-block reviewer is skipped for clearing") has no code behind it |
| One valid reviewer passes (D-2), `ledger.py:150-157, 273-275` | 1 valid empty block of 4 dispatched gives verdict PASS and exit 0; the round record holds `brief_ids, decision, doc_sha256, n, reviewers, verdict`, no quorum or completion field; the ledger never reads the manifest; only 0 valid of N refuses |
| Reviewer-typed inputs decide the verdict | CRITICAL with `blocking: false` is accepted (`findings.py:100-101` rejects only MINOR + blocking) and yields PASS; the reviewer's last line `verdict: FAIL` is ignored (never parsed); one blocking flag from any one reviewer fails the round; `confidence` is rendered, never read |
| Deferred row (D-11), `ledger.py:99-104, 235-238, 350-360` | a deferred row re-found as blocking stays `deferred`, round PASS, `brief_ids` empty; `defer` has no status guard and records no owner or expiry; a `defer` at the cap turns ESCALATE into PASS |
| Stored verdict (D-13), `ledger.py:363-372` | `verdict()` returns the stored last-round values; after `revise` the rows are `resolved_check` while `verdict()` still returns FAIL / REVISE (CLI exit 10) |
| Rounds | round 4 is accepted after ESCALATE at round 3 (only `n == len(rounds)+1` is checked); `--cap` is used only when round 1 creates the ledger |
| Span None | a row whose anchor is missing has `span None` and can never reach `resolved_check` by a fix (stays blocking until escalation) |
| `prior` lines | recorded as `prior_note` only; the row cleared through the clearing loop, not through the prior line |
| Re-review panel | all 8 packaged templates carry `"apply_to": ["first"]`; a re-review resolves ONE reviewer (`t1b-1`) by construction (`panel.py:600`) |

Tests pin these behaviours as intended: D-1 (`test_review_ledger.py:193-217`, `test_review_cli.py:274-292`), D-2 (`test_review_ledger.py:376-385`), D-11 (`:396-405`, `test_review_cli.py:298-313`; no test re-finds a deferred row), missing-anchor rows (`:408-417`), the narrow ref grammar (`test_review_findings.py:201-212`), reviewer re-classification (`test_review_ledger.py:518-546`). No test asserts `verdict()` after `apply_revision`, and none requires a quorum. A fix to any of them is a contract change that rewrites a test.

**Brief and input delivery (R05).** Five brief families deliver input four different ways: the review loop (candidate by `@file` plus sha256 in the brief; baseline and prior report by path; no driving document); the E2 harness (candidate path in a sandbox, `source.md` copied beside it but never named); the reflect shadow brief (`<output>/reviewer-briefs/reviewer-<N>.md`, three sections, spec body inline for the qa persona, input frozen in `artifacts/input-snapshot.yaml`); the code-driven reflect engine (tasklist body pasted between `<<<TARGET>>>` markers, no spec; `spec_path` reaches only the Tier-1 command line, `runner.py:471-472`); and `superclaude tasklist validate` (paths, roadmap yes, spec deliberately not: "VALIDATION LAYERING GUARD", own HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW vocabulary, `DEV-NNN` ids). Brief defects B-1 to B-5 and B-7 and the process-redesign briefs CB-1, CB-2, CB-4, CB-5 are still open at HEAD (B-6, `unpassable-ac`, was a harness-only typo that no shipped file carried). Twelve spec-shaped hard-codings are catalogued (R05 unit 7), among them: the reference-id regex in two files; the section-ref rule; the six categories copied in the prompt, the reflect brief and the harness; the five placeholders; the "requirement the document never states = Medium" grading paragraph; telemetry strata `("sonnet","haiku")` (`telemetry.py:112-115`); review kinds `("first","re-review")` in `panel.py:36` against `("first","re-review","audit")` in `telemetry.py:19`; RFC-2119 metrics; `PRIMARY_ROLES` per lens (`cluster.py:67-71`, already table-driven); the reflect cap inside the shared validator (`panel.py:71-73`); role-by-filename resolution in `card_convert.py:15-18, 466-470` (the plan is `<id>.md`, the spec is the entry named exactly `source.md`). The E2 `theory.py` HARD set (B3, B7 in; B5, I1, B6 out; by-kind definition) means the "not a thinking-budget ceiling" claim cannot be used as a fact: haiku, sonnet and grok rise within model in the same table, and the data file is not committed.

**Run record, manifest and telemetry (R15, [CODE-VERIFIED]).**

| Surface | Writer | Cost unit |
|---|---|---|
| `review-telemetry/1` JSONL plus SQLite (`telemetry.py`, 447 lines) | none in `src/` (the only caller of `append_record` is the manual CLI, `telemetry_cmd.py:67`); real writers exist in E3 experiment harnesses (`p20/live-evals/harness/harness.py:534-560`) | tokens in / cache / out and `wall_s` per reviewer session; no USD; no record kind for orchestrator, calibrator, debate, judge or validator |

| E2 result rows | five different schemas (`r1-results/1`, `r2-results/1`, `r3-result/1`, `r4-results/1`, none) | output tokens only; R5 alone per reviewer |

Verified properties: the telemetry schema rejects unknown keys at the top level and in each group and constrains only `context` values (`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$` or numbers); the claim "No document text ... ever enters a record" (`telemetry.py:3`) is a convention for the six groups. D-17: `model_scores` sums a run's `cost_tokens_out` once per live outcome (case: 1,000 tokens with two live outcomes gives 400 per TP, correct 200; supersession works). D-23: `manifest.save` is an atomic replace with no lock or version check; a deterministic interleaving loses reviewer-1's attempt (`reviewers_complete` 1 instead of 2); a real two-process race was not run and 29 real manifests show no lost attempt (9 lack `dispatched` attempts because `record_attempt` refuses once the stage is committed, `manifest.py:371`). `record_attempt` stores `{stage, reviewer_id, attempt_id, completion, payload_sha256}` and discards the payload; in shadow03 all six attempts carry the identical hash `83115a12...a516b2`. Concurrent LLM Read-and-Write of one memory file has the same unlocked shape (2.1).

**Defect register (R17).** 171 rows (170 distinct) from nine numbering schemes (263 original ids; 253 mapped, 10 claim checks, none lost), with one crosswalk to `DR-nnn`. Reproduction status: 64 REPRODUCED, 46 TRACED, 2 mixed, 59 UNVERIFIED, 0 NOT-REPRODUCED. Fix owner buckets: CORE 75 (74 distinct), MODULE-reflect 29, MODULE-tasklist 2, MODULE-spec 2, HARNESS 14, EVAL 36, OPS 2, DROP 11. Families the core owns, in R17's order of consequence: verdict and clearing rules (DR-002, 003, 008, 009, 107, 108, 112, 114); the silent drop and anchor family (DR-001, 004, 005, 006, 056-058, 060, 061, 113, 123); panel resolution (DR-014-018, 020, 071, 109, 111, 115, 125); brief and parser contract (DR-023-027, 029); persistence and CLI (DR-011-013, 043, 053-055, 059, 079, 126); telemetry (DR-021, 022, 110, 116, 117, 127); E1 additions (DR-118-121, 124, 146, 159, 162, 168, 171). About a dozen rows are pinned by tests as intended behaviour. Additional verified facts: the `@live7` template resolves a duplicate model in 30 of 40 gateway resolutions with run ids `run1..run40` (26 of 40 with `r1..r40`; both reproduced) and `@default` in 18 of 40; a fixed slot with `count > 1` resolves to the same model N times; `select_env` guesses the environment from `$T3Model01`; the Stage 2 exit test (`test_the_current_repository_reports_without_crashing`) accepts any documented exit code so a FAIL does not fail CI; `.gitignore:13` (`lib/`) silently excluded the E2 collaboration harness code.

**Corrections ([CODE-CONTRADICTED]).** Slice-level statements that `findings_v2` limits are "inherited through `_check_flat`" at `findings_v2.py:15-22` (lines 15-22 are the import block; the limits are literals at `:80, 111, 126, 132, 136`); slice references to a v2 `_check_finding` (the function is `check_finding`); the E2 note that findings-v1 `merge` is "unchanged" so the contract is one contract (HEAD has two). ### 2.6 Dispatch, tiers and model identity

**Tier data at HEAD (`src/superclaude/cli/review/data/review-tiers.default.json`, 38 lines).** [R04 s1, CODE-VERIFIED]

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| `aliases` | tier1a `claude-gw-tier1a[1m]` -> [claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5]; tier1b -> [claude-sonnet-5-5, gpt-6.1-sol, muse-wonder-full-1.0]; tier2 -> [gpt-6.1-sol, glm-5.3, grok-4.7, Qwen3.8-max, muse-wonder-1.0, muse-spark-1.3]; tier2b -> [gpt-6.1-terra, glm-5.3, Qwen3.8-max, muse-wonder-1.0]; tier3 -> [glm-5.3, Qwen3.8-max]; tier4 -> [gpt-6-luna, claude-haiku-5-5, grok-4.7]. No `tier0` alias; no `muse-ember-1.0` |
| `classes` | 13 model ids in 9 class names: opus, sonnet, haiku, fable, gpt, muse, glm, grok, qwen |
| `environments.gateway` | `available: all`, `stand_ins: {}`, `launch: {}`, note "dispatch mechanism per model not defined yet" |
| `environments.anthropic-only` | available opus, sonnet, haiku, fable; stand-in `claude-haiku-5-5` for tiers 2, 2b, 3, 4; `launch` maps a model id to a Claude Code class word |

The product `superclaude review` package only RESOLVES reviewers: its output holds per reviewer `model`, `alias`, `fallbacks`, `stand_in` and `launch` (a class word or `None`). The only subprocess call in the package is `git rev-parse` (`panel.py:19, 382, 392`); `alias` strings are data and no launcher reads them (R04 s3.1, Grep negative evidence).

**Five layers of tier data (R04 s5).**

| Layer | Where | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Coder workspace env (`aienv.d/defaults.sh`, outside the repo) | `T<N>Model0<M>` ids and `T<N>_WINDOW` |
| 2 | `src/superclaude/skills/ccsession-tag/ccsession-models.json` (181 lines) | tier name -> `models_env` slot NAMES (tier0 `T0Model01-02`, tier1a, tier1b, tier2 `T2Model01-06`, tier2b `T2bModel01-04`, tier3, tier4 `T4Model01-03`); no model ids, no `classes`, no `launch` |
| 3 | `src/superclaude/skills/ccsession-tag/MODEL-TIERS.md` (227 lines) | human table; the three places (env, JSON, this page) change together |
| 4 | `review-tiers.default.json` | the same lists as DATA, copied by hand, plus `classes`, `names`, `environments` |
| 5 | `local-gateway-alias-proxy.py` (shim) | turns `claude-gw-tierN[1m]` into a failover walk over that tier's env-defined models (`:819-839`) |

The only mechanical cross-check of Layer 4 is `tests/review/test_review_panel_live7.py:92-98`, which compares the COUNT of models for tier2b, tier3 and tier4 and the first model of tier2b and tier3; tier1a, tier1b and tier2 are not checked. The live workspace env (2026-11-14) has `T2Model01=gpt-6.1-sol`, `T2bModel01=gpt-6.1-terra`, `T3Model01=glm-5.3`, `T4Model01=gpt-6-luna`, `T4Model04=muse-ember-1.0`; "first model of the tier" is order-dependent and the order is owned by the Coder env file.

**Four dispatch mechanisms (R04 s3.5, [CODE-VERIFIED] / [OBSERVED-RUNTIME]).**

| Property | E1 Claude-orchestrated (skill) | E1 code-driven (swarm) | E2 harness | Product `review` package |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unit named at dispatch | a class word on the Agent `model` argument (or agent frontmatter `sonnet`) | raw model id in the HTTP body | raw model id on `--model` | none (resolution only) |
| Reaches a non-first model of a tier | no (class -> env alias -> tier alias -> first non-cooling model) | yes (`T2Model0N` pool) | yes | not applicable |
| Reviewer tools | read-only agent | none (plain completion) | Bash allowed; Edit, Write, NotebookEdit disallowed | not applicable |
| Served model recorded by | transcript only (`message.model` of sidechain) | not recorded | `OBS` from the transcript JSON (`run-reviewer.sh:51`) | not recorded |
| Model in contract or telemetry | class or pin | requested id (`openai_compat.py:467-470`; the response `model` field is never read) | expected and observed | intended id |

```
Orchestrator Agent call: model=haiku
  -> ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL = claude-gw-tier2[1m]      (ccsession:896-898 in a tier workspace)
  -> shim local-gateway-alias-proxy.py:694-697, _forward_tier (:834-839): first non-cooling model of tier2
  -> served: gpt-6.1-sol, not Claude Haiku                      (seen in comboA-r1 stream log: sidechain message.model)
Raw id request (E2):  claude -p --model <id>  -> shim named_fallback (:432-449): may be served by a later model of the same tier
```

Verified details: the Agent tool `model` enum accepts only `sonnet | opus | haiku | fable` (observed in this session's tool schema; E2's probe records "not usable for tier3 / tier4 / tier2b or non-first-slot models"); `reflect-reviewer`, `confidence-calibrator` and `evidence-validator` default to `model: sonnet` in frontmatter and `rf-qa.md` has no `model:` key; the code-driven engine builds `OpenAICompatTransport(base_url, api_key, model=model_id)` per model from the `T1Model0N` / `T2Model0N` pools (`ensemble.py:276-285`, `swarm/config.py:56-59`); `_diversity.py` and `compute_vendor_diversity` classify from the REQUESTED id. The E2 identity guard compares against `$MODEL`, which the fallback code overwrites (`run-reviewer.sh:76`), so a fallback is judged against itself. E3's loop names no launch mechanism: `document_review_loop_prompts.md:70` says to run each review "with the reviewers that `superclaude review panel resolve` prints ... each in a fresh context". `scripts/reflect_*.py` dispatch nothing (no subprocess or model call).

**Requested against served model.**
- Requested side is recorded in the resolution JSON (`reviewers[].model`, `launch`), the card header `model:` copied from `panel/resolution.json`, contract `reviewer_models`, and the parity recompute (`reflect_shadow_exit.py:117-177`, which compares requested to requested and never reads `model_observed`).
- Served side: Grep of `src/superclaude` finds `model_observed` only in the `model_scores` SQL view (`telemetry.py:364, 378`) and in SKILL.md prose (`:341`); no Python writer of a `model_observed` value exists. The orchestrator may write an extra `model_observed:` header line on instruction (69 card files across 11 of 15 combo run dirs; 10 under `.dev/reflect`); `identity_source: observed` appears in 1 of 15 combo contracts and 0 of 13 pilot contracts. The Claude Code Agent result carries `resolvedModel`, but its value is the environment-resolved REQUEST string (combo A-r1 haiku-class calls show `claude-gw-tier2[1m]` while the sidechain `message.model` was `gpt-6.1-sol`), so it is a collapse detector, not an identity proof; it is host behaviour not pinned in this repo ([UNVERIFIED] outside the stream logs).
- Collapse figures re-derived from `results.jsonl` and the 15 stream logs: A-r3 only (all 3 `reflect-reviewer` calls, 3 `confidence-calibrator` calls and 1 `evidence-validator` call carried no `model` argument; 37 sidechain assistant messages all `claude-sonnet-5-5`); so 1 of 3 tier3-orchestrated runs and 0 of 12 B-E runs. Pin against served differences by design of the combos: the haiku class served `gpt-6.1-sol` in 5 reviewer calls (A1, A2, B1, B2, B3), the opus class served `gpt-6-luna` in D1-D3 and E1-E3, the sonnet class served `claude-haiku-5-5` in E1-E3. The A-r3 contract reports `calibrator_diversity: full`, `identity_mismatch_suspected: false`, `reviewer_models: [claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-5-5, claude-opus-5-5]`: the collapse is invisible in every contract field.
- One failure class explains the E1 collapse: an Agent call with no `model` argument, a prompt-compliance failure of the orchestrator, not a tier-data fault.

**Three vocabularies for "class" (R04 s8).** The tier file's `classes` (9 names, used by `--hard-exclude-class`, the reflect profile and the parity check); the vendor substring table `_vendor_from_model_id` (`_diversity.py:39-61`: all Claude models are one vendor `anthropic`; `muse` and `llama` share `meta`; marker `o1` matches by substring); the SKILL.md class set `{opus, sonnet, haiku, qwen, kimi, deepseek}` (`SKILL.md:1248`, rotation at `:655`; `kimi` and `deepseek` appear in no tier list). "Class diversity" is counted three ways (distinct `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` strings in SKILL.md `:232-240` and `runner.py:291-310`; distinct succeeded `model_id` values in `_diversity.py`; the pinned resolution in shadow) and all three use requested values. When the three variables hold tier ids, tier1a and tier1b both list `claude-sonnet-5-5`, so a failover of tier1a to its second model would silently make the opus class and the sonnet class the same model.

**`T2bModel01` (R04 s6, Grep re-derived).** 18 line occurrences in 11 files: defined as a slot NAME at `ccsession-models.json:107`; read generically by ccsession through `models_env` (`models.py:666-672, 738-742`); read by name only in the implement retry-ladder prose (`sc-implement-protocol/refs/retry.md:162, 172`, rung 0); in tests (`test_ccsession_tiers.py:72-73, 239`, `test_workflow_archive.py:799`, `test_model_alias_policy.py:227`), in docs and the CHANGELOG. No panel code reads it: `panel.py:486-494` `select_env` reads `$T3Model01` only; the panel reaches tier 2b only through the `tier2b` alias entry. The E2 run-2 note "not referenced anywhere in src/ or tests/" is [CODE-CONTRADICTED] (4 `src` files, 3 `tests` files); its narrow form "panel code does not read it" is true.

**`muse-ember-1.0` (R04 s7).** Absent from `src`, `tests`, `docs`, `scripts`, `plugins`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `ccsession-models.json` (which lists only `T4Model01-03` for tier 4) and the installed copy of that JSON. It appears in E1 `PLAN.md:109, 194` as an absence note, in E2 evidence and harness (`run-reviewer.sh:26, 33-34`, "being added as Tier 04 Model 02"), and in the live workspace env as `T4Model04` and in `CCSESSION_MODEL_ORDER` (a picker order, not tier membership). ccsession and the shim read only the slots named in the JSON, so `T4Model04` is invisible to them. The E2 recommended default panel "ember + 2x luna" names a model the product tier file cannot resolve and the gateway environment cannot launch.

**Corrections ([CODE-CONTRADICTED]).** Scope slice 11 s5.3: every contract records `requested-pinned` (1 of 15 combo contracts records `observed`). `docs/reference/model-aliases.md:56` ("they did not exercise the Agent-call parameter") is out of date (combo A1 shows the Agent `model` argument honoured through the env aliases); `:26-28` omits the `[1m]` suffix that `ccsession:896-898` exports. Run-1 note quoting `MODEL-TIERS.md:42` ("if Terra returns 429 retried on GLM-5.3 (owner 2026-11-11)") is stale: `MODEL-TIERS.md:44` now describes the 2026-11-12 rule (the first two other 429s go back to Claude Code, the third parks Terra). `review-tiers.default.json:26` ("not defined yet") is true but has no ticket.

**Contradictions between research files.** None open for this subsection. R04 and R07 both derive the 1-of-3 / 0-of-12 collapse figures from the same logs and agree; R07 adds the calibrator collapse (6 of 15).

**Not verified (for Section 9).** The pilot dispatch-collapse "6 of 9" (logs gone) and whether the tier3-orchestrator effect is real (GQ-042); r1 and r2 launch models (GQ-043); host behaviour of the Agent `model` enum, `resolvedModel` and the family-alias edge case at `model-aliases.md:51` (GQ-044); whether the gateway serves `muse-ember-1.0` today and whether ember is Tier 4 slot 02 or 04 (GQ-046); who records the served model and from where (GQ-049); how the hand-kept tier lists stay in sync (GQ-050).

### 2.7 Consumers: tasklist, workflow, brainstorm, design, pr_submit and the rf-qa family

**Who drives the shared review machinery today (R12 s7, [CODE-VERIFIED] by grep counts).** Exactly two consumers use the findings, ledger and panel code: the spec-panel loop (through the prompts file that its hard gate names) and the reflect shadow path (through `sc-reflect-protocol`, 6 references in SKILL.md plus 1 in `document_review_loop_prompts.md`, 2 in `docs/reference/review-panel-live7.md`). Python importers of `superclaude.cli.review` are `cli/main.py:568, 570` and three E1 measurement scripts (`reflect_cluster_pairs.py`, `reflect_stage0a_replay.py`, `reflect_shadow_exit.py`). Brainstorm, design, workflow, tasklist, pr-submit, auggie-review, rf-qa, `/task` and `/sc:implement` each have their own review path that does not touch `cli/review` (the swarm lens registry was not read for overlap).

**Consumer map.**

| Consumer | Review mechanism today | Effect of a failing result | Reaches the panel? |

| `/sc:workflow` Wave 4 (`sc-workflow-protocol/SKILL.md:85-93`, 107 lines) | one `/sc:reflect --mode pre --spec <pkg>/source.md --tasklist <pkg>/<id>.md` call, defaults for every other flag, no `--remediate` (`:89`); `--unattended --output <report-dir>/nested/reflect-<n>/` variant (`:91`) | advisory and read-only: never edits the plan or changes `status`; reflect unavailable gives `reflect_status: skipped | failed` and `reflect_report_path: null`; contract keys `reflect_status` (closed enum success / partial / failed / skipped) and `reflect_report_path` (`refs/return-contract.md:16-21`) are read by workflow's eval companion test, `sc-troubleshoot-protocol`, `sc-auggie-review-protocol:348` and reflect's own handoff | no: `--t2-engine` is not passed, so the default `legacy` runs; Grep of `t2-engine` finds 8 files, none a workflow or tasklist file |
| `sc:tasklist` T1 Stage 6 self-check (`:1279-1290`) | 20 deterministic checks | blocking, pre-write | no |
| T2 Stage 7 roadmap validation (`:1347-1433`) | 2N parallel `Task` agents, `split = ceil(task_count/2)`, five dimensions (Drift, Contradictions, Omissions, Weakened criteria, Invented content), severity High / Medium / Low | at least one failed agent: a `synthetic-dnsp` HIGH per failed agent and proceed; zero succeed: terminal | no |
| T3 Stages 8-10 patch loop (`:1435-1615`) | `sc:task --compliance strict` applies fixes; at most ONE re-patch pass (2 total passes, "NOT task-builder's 3-cap") | unresolved High or Medium at termination HALTs; under `--unattended` resolves as `blocked`; Medium is blocking here | no |

| T5 per-phase terminal task (`:1131-1189`) | `superclaude reflect run <phase-tasklist> --depth deep --fix --no-promote --base <PHASE_N_START_SHA> --output ...` | only wrapper exit 0 completes it; it also fails at exit 0 on a non-`pass` derived verdict, subrun `partial` / `failed`, convergence below 0.80, or drift or regression above 0 | engine A, no `--t2-engine`, no panel |
