**Severity vocabularies (R12 s2, [CODE-VERIFIED]).** The repo's canonical review rule `output-styles/pragmatic.md:224-231` is binary (blocking or minor; Medium is a warning among minor findings; at most 2 fix cycles; copied verbatim into ten primitives and pinned by `test_review_severity_rule.py:181-210, 320-339`).

| Vocabulary | Where | Blocking rule |
|---|---|---|
| CRITICAL / MAJOR / MINOR plus `blocking` boolean | `findings.py:14, 96-101`, spec-panel, loop prompts | CRITICAL blocks; MAJOR and FR-8/FR-9 block only with a concrete wrong outcome; a MAJOR with `blocking: false` is legal in the parser; with `reflect_category` set v2 forces `blocking == severity != MINOR` |
| CRITICAL / IMPORTANT / MINOR | `rf-qa.md:111`, `pragmatic.md:229` | CRITICAL and IMPORTANT block |
| High / Medium / Low | tasklist skill Stage 7 (`:1386`) | High and Medium block |
| HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW | tasklist CLI (`cli/tasklist/prompts.py`, `gates.py`) | only `high_severity_count == 0` gates |
| Critical / High / Medium / Low / Nit | `pr_submit/models.py:106-113`, auggie rubric | tiers carry routes, not a verdict (Critical / High `--depth deep --fix`, Medium `--fix`, Low / Nit report-only); Codex hints P0-P3 are input only |
| blocking / minor / note | `sc-implement-protocol/refs/qa.md:35-56` | derived from four yes/no answers |
| HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW deviation table | `reflect-reviewer.md:69-99` (plus lowercase 5-value `severity_hint` in `auggie-reviewer.md`) | class decides gating |

By distinct label sets R12 counts six sets plus two orthogonal axes (priority at `spec-panel.md:123`; reflect deviation class) and one input-only hint set. "Medium" has at least six distinct uses: non-blocking warning under `follow-up candidates` (spec-panel); a priority label (`spec-panel.md:123`); a PR tier whose route is `--fix`; BLOCKING in the tasklist skill (Stages 7-10); counted but not gated in the tasklist CLI; and a word `card_convert` maps, with `important` and `should-fix`, to MINOR non-blocking (`card_convert.py:81-82`; `important` is blocking under the rf-qa scale). Categories: six spec categories in `cli/review` (findings-v2 maps reflect categories onto the same six) against 18 PR categories with floor and ceiling in `severity_router.py:34-53`; the two sets share no member. Caps in the repo's unit (fix cycles): the master loop, rf-qa, `/task`, pr-submit's default and (on R12's reading of `sc-tasklist-protocol/SKILL.md:1604-1615`) the tasklist P2 loop agree on 2; the outliers are pr-submit's configurable hard cap of 5 and `/sc:implement`'s exempt ladder. Stop rules differ in kind (fail-closed verdict text, computed exit codes, monotonicity and regression halts, push predicates, score thresholds).

**Plugin mirror (R12 s5.3, R18 s7, [CODE-VERIFIED]).** `plugins/superclaude/` is hand-maintained (125 tracked files), not produced by `make sync-dev`, and shipped in the wheel (`pyproject.toml:78-87`). Skills present: `confidence-check`, `sc-implement-protocol`, `sc-recommend`, `sc-workflow-protocol`; there is no `sc-reflect-protocol`, `sc-tasklist-protocol`, brainstorm, adversarial, pr-submit or auggie-review skill, and no rf-*, `reflect-reviewer`, `auggie-reviewer` or `evidence-validator` agent. `plugins/.../design.md` differs from `src` by 57 changed lines and `brainstorm.md` by 16; the plugin brainstorm command tells the agent to invoke a skill the plugin does not ship; in a plugin install workflow Wave 4 calls a skill the plugin lacks and, by the rule at `SKILL.md:93`, ends as `reflect_status: skipped|failed` (inference from two verified facts, not executed).

### 2.8 Evaluation harness, governance and repository constraints

**A. Where the evaluation code lives (R16 part 5, [CODE-VERIFIED]).**

**Classification definitions (R01 section 4.1, applied to the row as a whole).**

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| identical | the efforts carry the same mechanism or the same code (shared code counts) |
| superset | one effort does everything the other does and adds at least one named capability. "Strict" = no capability of the smaller one is missing from the larger one. |
| conflicting | the efforts do the same job in an incompatible way (different vocabulary, schema, rule or semantics), so both cannot be the shared default without a decision |
| unique-E1 / unique-E2 / unique-E3 | only that effort has the mechanism; no incompatibility with the others is implied |

**How one row gets one class.** The class in the Classification column is the primary, decision-relevant relation, chosen in this order: conflicting (any [CODE-VERIFIED] incompatibility between two mechanisms of the row, including E3s against E3i) before superset before identical before unique. Secondary relations are written in the Notes column and feed the lists in 2.9.5 and 2.9.6. A cell that has no mechanism for the capability is written ABSENT. R01 used a fifth cell label "absent"; it is kept here for the same reason (an absent cell cannot be identical, superset, conflicting or unique). A mechanism that does the neighbouring job (for example E3i's blind `finding-grader` against calibration) is named in the cell as "adjacent" and still counts as ABSENT for that row.

**Evidence tags (rule 7 of the assignment).** `[CODE-VERIFIED]` = confirmed at file:line, by a read-only command or by a probe in the research file named. `[CODE-CONTRADICTED]` = the research file shows the code differs from a claim; the cell states what the code shows. `[UNVERIFIED]` = taken from a scope slice and not re-derived by the research file; it is flagged in the cell, never used as the sole basis of a class, and listed in 2.9.8 for Open Questions. A dagger (†) in the Evidence tag column marks a row with at least one [UNVERIFIED] cell. All 16 rows carry it (mostly E3i cells and E2 study figures), so it does not discriminate between rows; the Evidence tag column names which cells are [CODE-VERIFIED]. The class of rows 12, 14 and 15 (unique-E1, unique-E1, unique-E2) rests in part on an [UNVERIFIED] statement about another effort (E2 has no calibrator; E2 has no memory; E2 ground truth and blind judge exist only in E2), and is flagged again in 2.9.8.

**Row count.** The assignment lists 16 capabilities. R01 grouped "ids, identity and hash" into one row; here "Ids" (row 2) and "Identity and hash" (row 3) are separate rows so that each of the 16 named capabilities has its own row. Row 2 and row 3 content comes from R01 section 4.3 row 2 and R04 section 4; no fact is added.

**Path shorthand.** `RV` = `src/superclaude/cli/review`. `SKILL.md` without a prefix = `src/superclaude/skills/sc-reflect-protocol/SKILL.md`. Line numbers are those the research files cite at HEAD `50d4d2b9d` unless the cell says E2 tip.

#### 2.9.10 Key Takeaways of Section 2.9

- The 16-row matrix classifies 11 rows conflicting, 1 identical (Ids), 2 unique-E1 (Calibration, Memory) and 2 unique-E2 (Eval harness, Collaboration); no row is a primary superset and none is unique-E3 (Table A). The only [CODE-VERIFIED] strict superset is E1 over E3s on the panel engine (SS-1), and that engine is already one shared code base.
- The efforts agree on very little: one id pattern, the findings-v1 grammar as used by E2, the cap constant 3, and `contract.parse_contract` / `derive_verdict` as the only code shared by E1's two engines. Everything else the efforts share is a conflict that needs a decision: 21 conflicts are logged (CF-01 to CF-21).
- E1's clustering is not a strict superset of E3s's: its v2 clusters citation-located findings only, so anchor-located findings (spec and tasklist review) form singletons (CF-13, RC-2).
- No product code records the served model; every diversity, parity and identity field is computed from requested values, and engine A's diversity is over requested ids, not served ids (RC-1).
- E2 contributes no product code at any commit; it is the only source of ground truth, of the non-Claude dispatch that works today (`claude -p --model <raw id>` with a served-model check), and of the five collaboration designs, whose evidence is single smoke rows with `lib/` missing from the commit for r2-r5.
- Twelve of 48 cells carry no mechanism (E1 2, E2 6, E3 4); E2 reuses E3s unchanged for schema, ids and merge (3 cells) (Table B).
- 18 [UNVERIFIED] items are listed for Open Questions (2.9.8); the largest group is the E3i cells, which no research file re-derived beyond file existence, sizes, `SCHEMA`, `CAP_REVIEWS` and imports. Three classifications (rows 12, 14, 15) rest in part on an [UNVERIFIED] statement about E2.
- Eleven claims in the sources were [CODE-CONTRADICTED] and are corrected in Table E2 (CC-1 to CC-11); five statements differ between research files (or upgrade a tag), and for each the stronger evidence is named in Table E1 (RC-1 to RC-5, with RC-1 changing a row: R06's "served model_id" is wrong, R04 shows it is the requested id).

#### R1 2.1 E1: reflect Tier 2 panel kernel and shadow mode

**What E1 is.** The reflect Tier 2 panel kernel is a set of dormant, telemetry-only review tools plus a ten-step shadow recipe in the reflect skill. The kernel code is already on `origin/master` (commit d2d8a2d16, #519, Stage 0-2 of the Tier 2 review panel); the branch `ironbelly/shadow-runs` is three commits ahead (9874d63fb, c2e3347d3, 792cf8c52) at the time of run 1; HEAD `ad8f57560` is now 5 commits past merge-base `d2d8a2d16`, and the two skill-fix commits touch only four files: `SKILL.md` (inside §4.3a shadow steps 2, 4, 7, 10 and the §9.2 `findings_block_compliance_rate` comment), `refs/reviewer-spec.md` (the shadow instruction line :39) and two tests (R1-S03 baseline note and §1.1 [CODE-VERIFIED via `git diff`]; R1-S02 header). The kernel is therefore master code that E1 authored, not branch-only code. <!-- Variant 1 (modified) — M-25: stale 'three commits ahead' -->

**How it works: the authoritative legacy path (default, `--t2-engine legacy`).** The orchestrator composes two or three `reflect-reviewer` agents by model-class rotation and persona (analyzer, qa, refactorer or architect), writes three-section briefs, dispatches, persists cards, runs one blind `confidence-calibrator` per card (one card-level number), then merges by `sc-adversarial-protocol` Mode A (`--depth standard`, convergence score routing PASS at 0.75 or more, PARTIAL at 0.60 or more), runs the `evidence-validator` gate, and writes the 1.8.0 `return-contract.yaml` (R1-S03 §2.2; R1-R07 §1). The skill-path contract has no code writer; the orchestrator writes it (R1-R13 §4 [CODE-VERIFIED by absence], resolving R1-R08 gap 5). The wrapper degrades any Tier 2 run whose convergence score is below 0.80 or null and halts on any regression or drift count above zero (`contract.py:317-326`, `:377-381`; R1-R07 §8, R1-R05 §1).

**How it works: shadow mode (`--t2-engine shadow`, UC-1 pre only; accepted and ignored for UC-2).** Shadow runs next to the legacy steps and changes no verdict, no stable field and no `merge_method`; all panel files go under `<output>/panel/` and all fields under `telemetry:` (R1-S03 §2.3). The ten steps are: resolve and freeze (`review panel resolve --template @reflect-pre ... --strict-distinct`, then `review manifest init`), parity check, briefs plus one findings-v2 instruction line (`reviewer-spec.md:39`), normalise with a bounded re-ask, per-finding calibration line, `review cluster` plus `review verify-citations`, the legacy debate then a written `adversarial/merged-verdict.yaml`, a kept-ids cluster pass after the evidence validator, an identity check, publish (R1-S03 §2.3, SKILL.md :338-349). Shadow is a prose recipe the orchestrator follows; `cli/reflect/` holds no shadow code (R1-R07 §10; R1-S04 §0.8 doc-sourced, spot-checked by R1-R07).

**Identity and dispatch (dated 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13).** The panel record pins models; it does not observe them. Spike S-ID (3 probes, 2026-11-12) found self-report matched the pin 0 of 3 times and transcript `message.model` honoured 2 of 3 pins: a `haiku` pin ran `gpt-6.1-sol` because the gateway tier2 alias has no Anthropic model first; the Agent tool result does not expose the served model, only the sidechain transcript on disk does (R1-S04 §0.7). `identity_source: observed` has no implementation (R1-R04 R1-G2 [CODE-CONTRADICTED as an implemented feature]); the `model_observed:` card line is consumed by nothing (R1-R04 R1-G3); the only served-model extraction is the offline `extract.py:42-79` of the combination study (R1-R08 §10). A missing class collapsed a whole panel to Sonnet in the combination runs (R1-R04 summary). The `gateway` environment has `launch: {}`, so every reflect template fails to resolve there, and `anthropic-only` is not anthropic-only at serving time (R1-R04 summary; GQ R1-O-2).

**The 5x3 model-combination experiment (runs 2026-11-13).** Five combinations by three repeats under `.dev/eval-workspaces/shadow-model-combos/` (`PLAN.md`, `FINDINGS.md`, `results.md`, `combos.json`, `analysis/extract.py` 193 lines). It yields leads (orchestrator speed, confidence shift, compliance) at n=3 and no quality answer: blind ground-truth scoring was not approved or run. Combo A's orchestrator was served by GLM 5.3 and Qwen3.8-max, the same models the E2 study banned, which is a likely driver of its leads; `combos.json` `status: "designed, not run"` is stale because all 15 runs exist (R1-R11 §9, §12 gaps). The untracked `runs/pre-TASK-WF-designSpec-20261107-075614-comboC-r3/artifacts/base-e8db2fe6/` folder is an orchestrator-made base-commit archive, not a reviewer escaping its snapshot, and makes run C3 protocol-different (R1-R11 §10 summary). Per-run cost and served identity exist only in `extract.py`, derived from the outer session log, never in the product record (R1-R08 §10).

**Defects and constraints found.** Contract 1.8.0 is frozen: any new `merge_method` value or new top-level key fails `panel_lint` and needs a version bump, so the shared core can own resolution, cards, clustering, citation checks, calibration coverage and manifests (all telemetry) but not the merge decision or contract writer without a bump (R1-R07 summary). EV-1 is self-attested: the verdict file it reads is written by the same orchestrator (R1-R07 gap, GQ R1-G-13). The calibrator agent implements a 6-dimension troubleshoot rubric with a gated-minimum formula and reflect passes no `rubric_path`, so the claim "re-grades per the 5-dim reflection rubric" is [CODE-CONTRADICTED] (R1-R05 §4.1). Drift halts at any severity (`contract.py:380-381`) while findings-v2 forbids MINOR blocking (`findings_v2.py:107-108`) (R1-R05 §13). `unauthorized_deviation_present` has no producer rule anywhere in the skill (R1-R05 gap, GQ R1-G-03). Pins R1-C1, R1-C6 and R1-C14 compare against `HEAD`, so they guard only uncommitted edits (R1-R07 §10 Q5, R1-R12 §6).

#### R1 2.2 E2: tasklist review-panel evaluation study (commit 4a22d742)

**What E2 is.** An evaluation harness and a measured study, not product code. The hand-off states the branch changes no product code (`git diff origin/master...HEAD -- src tests` empty; doc-sourced, R1-S00 §0) and the inventory of the commit lists only study files under `.dev/eval-workspaces/tasklist-review-panel/` (R1-S01 §1; R1-R09 gap 12). The study scored 106 panel runs (rows; 62 distinct reviewer-model sets, including 3 pilot arms and 30 pre-source rows), of which 71 are valid-era rows (213 row-packages, 665 individual reviewer runs; "reviewer run" means one reviewer in one row and is used only for that unit below) against 3 plan packages with 16 known defects taken from real `/sc:implement` failures: `TASK-WF-designSpec-20261107-075614` (10 known, 5 blocking in implement), `TASK-WF-makeTheAliasOnly-20261105-051649` (4 known, 3 blocking) and the control `TASK-WF-design-20261108-041415` (2 known, 0 blocking) (R1-S00 §2.1; R1-R11 §4). It reviews tasklist first reviews only: one round, no reviser, no re-review (R1-S00 §2.7).

**Model-by-role observations (dated, one gateway).** `claude-sonnet-5-5` never had findings dropped at merge (446 of 446 kept) and read `source.md` in 62 of 63 runs (`gpt-6.1-terra` and `gpt-6.1-sol` also lost none, 103 of 103 and 8 of 8 kept, and opened `source.md` in 44 of 44 and 3 of 3 runs, but their reviews are empty or incomplete; `audit-D/summary.md:18`, `COMBO-REPORT.md:373`); `gpt-6-luna` is fast and thin with the weakest anchor fidelity (91.4% verbatim, 30 findings lost at merge); `muse-ember-1.0` is cheap, with 33 findings lost (the per-model counts include all dropped findings, not only blocking ones, R1-S01 summary correction (d)); `gpt-6.1-terra` and `gpt-6.1-sol` return empty or incomplete reviews; `glm-5.3` was slow in the pilot (805-1435 s per review, `combos/SPEC.md:5`) and the owner removed it from batch 4 onward for delays (`combos/SPEC.md:98`), so no source-era glm data exists (the "adds nothing" and "800-1800 s" wording sits in `COMBO-REPORT.md` lines the file declares superseded and is not carried); `Qwen3.8-max` timed out 3 of 4 runs and was excluded by the owner yet is still listed in the packaged `tier2` (4th of 6), `tier2b` (3rd of 4) and `tier3` (2nd of 2) lists (R1-S00 §2.3; R1-R04 §8; order read from `review-tiers.default.json` at HEAD 792cf8c52; a gateway `live7` resolution can draw it into two slots, R1-D11). <!-- Variant 1 (modified) — M-25: Qwen3.8-max '3 of 3 slots' corrected to '3 of 4 runs' -->

**Strategies that worked and failed (doc-sourced lessons).** Worked: blind scoring with an independent re-judge of 12 rows (12 of 12 agreement); ground truth from real implement failures with a `blocking_in_implement` flag; six read-only integrity audits after the data was in; replicates before any claim; an observed-model check on every run with quarantine instead of deletion; `NOFALLBACK=1` for evaluation runs; counting by agents and by a direct script (R1-S00 §3). Failed: single-run claims, per-reviewer attribution of merged rows, treating judge-blocking as real blocking, many concurrent gateway workers (model-identity bleed), a cyclic fallback ladder that hid wrong-model runs, not shipping `source.md` from the start (R1-S00 §3).

**Defects in the E2 harness itself (code-verified in R1-R11, R1-R08).** `expected_model` is overwritten on fallback (`run-reviewer.sh:58` with `:76`) and `final-table.py:44` groups panels by it; the cost glob also sums stale attempt files (`run-reviewer.sh:87`); `BLOCK_OK` greps the fence only, so invalid lines are invisible to the runner (:57); Bash is not denied under `bypassPermissions` (:48); the judge is blind to reviewer ids but not to panel name (`judge-one.sh:21`); a judge that exits 0 without `score.json` is silently dropped (`final-table.py:48`); the audit filter silently disappears when `/tmp/audit-*/flags.tsv` is missing (`final-table.py:24`); `three-way.py:4` executes a `/tmp` copy of `final-table.py`; audits A and D read attempt transcripts that are not committed (1.48 GB left out by owner order) and hard-code another worktree's paths, so they cannot be re-run from the commit (R1-R11 §1-3; R1-R08 §8, §12). The study bypassed `superclaude review panel resolve` (raw model ids, bash ladder), while its own `resolution-*.json` inputs show Qwen3.8-max and glm-5.3 twice in one `@live7` panel, so the hand-off claim that R1-D11 was "not observed in the eval" is [CODE-CONTRADICTED] in data (R1-R11 §4, R1-R04 summary).

**Product-code defects E2 reported.** R1-D1 to R1-D16 against the shared review package are summarised with their current-code status in section 2.4 (R1-S02 §5, R1-S00 §2.4). All 16 hand-off defects that touch the package were confirmed at current code, with line numbers for R1-D7, R1-D11 and R1-D12 moved (R1-D11 now `panel.py:536-543`, R1-D12 `panel.py:485-494`, R1-D7 `telemetry.py:23` and `findings.py:29`) (R1-S02 §5, R1-R04 §10 stale docs, R1-R03 stale docs).

#### R1 2.4 The shared review CLI package: two stacks in one package

**Shape.** `src/superclaude/cli/review/` is one click group (`superclaude review`, registered at `cli/main.py:568-570`) that holds two parallel stacks. The #346 v1 stack [E3] (`findings` to `ledger` to `merge_cmd` and `ledger_cmd`, plus `telemetry`; 131 tests) produces verdicts. The reflect v2 stack [E1] (`findings_v2` to `card_convert` and `cluster` to `cluster_cmd` and `verify_cmd`, plus `manifest`; 520 tests) is telemetry and flagging only. `panel.py` is shared by both. The package on this branch equals `origin/master` (d2d8a2d16): `git log d2d8a2d16..HEAD -- src/superclaude/cli/review tests/review` is empty (R1-S02 header). There are seven real subcommands (`panel resolve|validate`, `merge`, `ledger revise|defer|verdict|capture`, `telemetry taskvars|append|load`, `cluster`, `verify-citations`, `manifest init|advance|validate`) plus two ghost loader names, `lint_cmd` and `estimate_cmd`, which belong to unmerged experiment branches PN2 and PN3; the loader swallows the missing module silently; each of the seven real subcommands has its own help-presence test (`test_review_cli.py:44-49` for `panel`, `merge`, `ledger`, `telemetry`; `test_review_cluster_cmd.py:260`; `test_review_verify_citations.py:194`; `test_review_manifest.py:434-439`), but no test pins the exact registered set or the absence of the ghost names (R1-R09 §1 [CODE-VERIFIED]; help tests re-read at HEAD 792cf8c52; R1-D13).

```

**The third merge path: the code-driven Tier 2 engine behind the blocking post gate [E1-adjacent: master baseline].** `superclaude reflect run` accepts only `--depth standard|deep` (`commands.py:255`), and `runner.py:538-545` always calls `run_tier2_ensemble` for those depths and then sets `rc = 0` unconditionally, so the `/sc:reflect` skill, its 1.8.0 contract, `panel_lint` and the shadow kernel are never involved in the gate (R1-R13 §2.1, §2.4 [CODE-VERIFIED]). Provenance contradiction: the task scheme tags `cli/reflect/` code [E1], but `git diff --stat origin/master` over `ensemble.py`, `runner.py`, `contract.py`, `commands.py`, `config.py` is empty and `git log` shows PRs #213, #214, #220 and #329, so the engine predates the E1 shadow work and is master baseline; the stronger evidence is the diff, so this file calls it E1-adjacent (R1-R13 §1.7).

| Property | What the code does | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Reviewers | in-process transport calls to external OpenAI-compatible models from the `T2Model0N` env pool (swarm package), no tools; they see only a header with the base ref plus the tasklist body, no diff and no code under audit; an `OSError` yields an empty body | `ensemble.py:339`, `:601-630`; R1-R13 §1.5 |
| Merge | mechanical concatenation, then a score-only `/sc:adversarial` child that returns `convergence_score` only | `ensemble.py:514-561`, `:633-654`; R1-R13 §1.5 |
| Contract | writes its own version-`"1.0"` `return-contract.yaml` with 11 keys outside the 1.8.0 lists (`REFLECT_CONTRACT_VERSION` :74; `yaml.safe_dump` :886-895); `merge_method` is `adversarial` whenever two or more reviewers succeed, even if the adversarial step failed (:773); `status` is the literal `"success"` (:789) | R1-R13 §1.6, §3-4 |
| Verdict | deviation fields default clean (:103-113, :442-471), so no production contract can HALT on a found deviation; the gate is a reviewer-agreement and diversity check, not a deviation audit | R1-R13 §10 R1-D1 (graded Critical) |
| Missing steps | no calibration, no evidence validation (`citations_dropped` is the constant 0, :817), no clustering, no reviewer cards | R1-R13 §1.5 |
| Executor exclusion | `executor_model_class` is read from phase-file frontmatter (`config.py:53`, `:351-354`) but the Tier 2 route never uses it; the gate's "executor-disjoint reviewers" claim (`sc-tasklist-protocol/SKILL.md:1165`, `:1177`) is [CODE-CONTRADICTED] | R1-R13 §2.4, §6 |
| Fix loop | `--fix` is inert on this route: the ensemble contract carries no remediation keys | `runner.py:762-775`; R1-R13 §2.2 |
| Failure surface | an exception in the engine re-raises and exits 1, outside the documented 0/10/11/2 map (`commands.py:442-469`); `REPORT.md` and the per-task verdict matrix the gate text promises are never produced | R1-R13 §2.4, §6, §10 |
| Tests | `tests/cli/reflect/test_ensemble_*` (2036 lines); tests patching `runner.ClaudeProcess` never exercise the engine through the runner | R1-R13 §2.1, §7 |

Two reflect contract schemas therefore share one file name and one reader (`contract.py`): the skill's 1.8.0 contract written by the orchestrator and this engine's code-written "1.0" (R1-R13 gap 15, R1-R08 §12).

**Callers of the review CLI today.** Grep over skills, commands and core (2026-11-14): `review merge` and `review ledger revise` are named only in `document_review_loop_prompts.md:70`; `ledger defer|verdict|capture` have no prose caller; `review panel resolve` is called by reflect shadow step 1 (`SKILL.md:340`) and prompts :70; `cluster`, `verify-citations` and `manifest` only by reflect shadow steps and offline scripts; `telemetry *` and `panel validate` by tests only (R1-R09 §7 [CODE-VERIFIED]). The earlier statement that no skill calls `panel resolve` is [CODE-CONTRADICTED] (GQ R1-CLS-12).

**Known gaps in the PR and rf-qa consumers (current state, not design).** The PR router differs from its rubric on at least seven points (rubric `in_diff` exception versus an unconditional tier drop at `severity_router.py:178-189`; no `error-handling` row in the router or the rubric; `security-latent` exists only in the router; `tests` floor Medium versus the rubric's calibration example Low; step 5 drops every finding when `deep=True` and no caller passes it; low-confidence Critical drop unconditional; fixed ceilings), most of them dormant for live Augment and Codex roots because those carry only a severity hint, not `category`, `confidence` or `in_diff` (R1-R10 §2, §1.3; the classifier's added fields are [UNVERIFIED]). `rf-qa.md:41` still says a QA pass that finds zero issues is suspect, which conflicts with the #346 no-quota rule, and the test docstring that claims the wording was removed is [CODE-CONTRADICTED] (the test bans only "surfaces zero issues as suspect", `test_review_prompt_overrides.py:146`) (R1-R10 §4). Replacing rf-qa also touches three test files that pin rf-qa text (R1-S05 §1C; R1-R12 §7).

## 3. Target State

Sources: research files `01-*.md` to `18-*.md` and `gaps-and-questions.md` under `.dev/tasks/to-do/TASK-RESEARCH-review-panel-run2-20261114-075454/` (research files are in its `research/` folder; cited below as `R01` to `R18`, `GQ`). Only [CODE-VERIFIED] items are stated as current fact; [UNVERIFIED] items are flagged in place and listed in the carry-over block 4.6 at the end of this file (owner decisions, [UNVERIFIED] claims, stale-documentation clusters) for Section 9. Section 3 is the Target State, Section 4 the Gap Analysis, with sub-blocks 4.1 to 4.6.

Programs: E1 = reflect Tier 2 panel kernel, shadow mode and the 5x3 model-combination experiment (merged #519 plus evidence commits on `ironbelly/shadow-runs`). E2 = tasklist review-panel study, collaboration and process-redesign designs on `origin/ironbelly/eval-tasklist-review-panel` (tip 6c0984326cbb8fb06c4a36065de58b171d3f8175; no product code at any commit, R01 s1.1). E3 = the #346 review loop: E3s = shipped source (`src/superclaude/cli/review` v1 path, `spec-panel.md` Review Loop, loop prompts); E3i = installed-only variants under `~/.claude`.

Severity rubric used in Section 4 (stated once; derived from the task's rule C8 and the research evidence, not invented findings): Critical = the target state cannot hold until this is decided or fixed, or it is a verdict that fails open, or an unwired in-scope capability (rule C8, marked "C8"). Important = the target holds but loses value, correctness or evidence quality without it. Minor = documentation, naming or cosmetic divergence.

Question this section answers (research question context): which ONE unified central Review Panel design captures all the value of E1, E2 and E3 and keeps future PR code review and rf-qa replacement unblocked. Everything below is derived from the research files; items that depend on an owner decision are marked "decision" and listed in the Section 9 carry-over at the end of this file. This section states the target, not a plan: no sequencing, branches, PRs, risks or estimates.

**Precedence between Sections 3 and 4 and Section 7 (read this first).** Sections 3 and 4 were written from the research files before the 15 adjudication debates of item 5.50 were folded into Section 7. Where a target statement in Section 3 (3.1 to 3.5, the success criteria SC-01 to SC-33) or a Target State cell in Section 4 differs from an adjudicated outcome in Section 7 (7.0, 7.0.1, 7.1, the axes table, the choices table A-3 to A-20 and the register), **Section 7 governs**, and the Section 3 or 4 wording is withdrawn, narrowed or replaced as the table below states. The table adds no decision: every right-hand cell is copied in substance from the Section 7 text named in it. It lists the items found by a comparison of the 7.0, 7.0.1 and 7.1 text with Sections 3 and 4; it is not a second review of every row, and a gap in Section 4 keeps its severity as a statement about today's code even when its target cell is replaced here.

### 3.5 Target-shaping decisions still open

The target above holds under every option of the decisions below; they change its detail, not its shape. They are carried in full to Section 9 (see the carry-over block at the end of this file): default finding locator; verdict authority and quorum; one ledger vocabulary; fixed severity pair versus module-declared severity sets (R12 and R13 disagree, see the contradiction table); class versus raw-id dispatch; which reflect engine's path the shared core serves; DO4 entry point; ground truth and acceptance rule; whether collaboration is in the first shape.

- **Desired behavior:** One central Review Panel made of a shared core plus thin per-use-case modules. The shared core is the `src/superclaude/cli/review/` package (E3 v1 stack plus the E1 v2 stack) extended with: one finding contract with pluggable lens namespaces, one clusterer, one merge and verdict stage that separates "candidate" from "blocking", one run record, one code-rendered brief template, and a resolver that declares distinctness and records observed identity. Each thin module owns only what differs per consumer: lens name, severity scale and category map, primary location kind, id grammar, blocking predicate, brief slot values, and the advisory-or-blocking policy. The core serves five consumers (below). This is a target derived from the research design inputs (`research/02` section 9, `03` Q9, `04` section 10, `06` section 6, `08` section 11.3, `09` section 8, `10` section 5, `01` section 18); no research file shows it implemented.

#### R1 3.1 External context used by Section 3 (web research, not codebase fact)

| Topic | Finding | Source URL | Reliability noted by the research |
|---|---|---|---|
| Union vs weighted voting | Any-reviewer ("union") voting: 82.7% recall, 85.0% false-positive rate vs weighted voting 37.7% recall, 35.3% FPR (vulnerability detection). | https://arxiv.org/html/2602.17875v1 | preprint, Feb 2026 [external context, `web-01`] |
| LLM validators | Validators confirm but rarely reject (TPR above 96%, TNR below 25%); a calibrated minority veto beat majority vote. | https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11822v2 | preprint, Oct 2025 [external context, `web-01`] |
| Panels vs single judge | Heterogeneous panels beat one large judge on average (PoLL), but judge errors are correlated (9 judges gave about 2 effective votes). | https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.18796 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2605.29800v1 | [external context, `web-01`, `web-03`] |
| Debate vs meta-judge | Debate amplifies judge bias after round one; meta-judge aggregation is more resistant (accuracy not measured). | https://arxiv.org/html/2505.19477v3 | EMNLP 2025 Findings [external context, `web-01`] |
| Production review systems | Reviewers propose; a coordinator or verifier deduplicates, verifies against source and applies a severity rubric before anything blocks; singletons are verified, not discarded. | https://blog.cloudflare.com/ai-code-review ; https://www.linkedin.com/blog/engineering/ai/high-signal-ai-code-review-that-adapts-to-your-codebase-at-scale ; https://cursor.com/blog/building-bugbot | vendor first-party, no error rates [external context, `web-01`] |
| Severity interchange | SARIF `level` has three buckets (error, warning, note) and `rank` 0-100 is the lossless order; every 3-to-5 or 5-to-3 mapping loses a tier at the extremes; the middle tier is kept distinct everywhere except our `card_convert` (`medium` to MINOR). | https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/sarif-v2.1.0.html ; https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/code-scanning/sarif-files/sarif-support | official standard and vendor docs [external context, `web-02`] |
| Finding identity across commits | GitHub code scanning matches alerts only via `partialFingerprints.primaryLocationLineHash` plus rule id and path; an empty hash degrades to order-based matching. Transitive closure has high recall and poor precision ("black hole" clusters); complete-link or size caps are the documented remedies. | https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/code-scanning/sarif-files/sarif-support ; https://github.com/github/codeql-action/blob/main/src/fingerprints.ts | official docs and source [external context, `web-04`] |
| Judge calibration | Self-preference and same-family bias are real but partly an artefact; verbalized numeric confidence is weakly discriminative; no controlled study of heterogeneous panels for defect-finding or spec review was found, so the project's own labelled packages are the validation set. | https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22548 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2611.01829v1 | preprints [external context, `web-03`] |

## 4. Gap Analysis


Columns: `Gap | Current State | Target State | Severity | Notes`. Evidence file paths are given in Notes. Gap ids are G-nn. The Target State cells state the pre-adjudication target: where a cell differs from an adjudicated outcome in Section 7, Section 7 governs, and the delta table at the head of Section 3 names the cells concerned (G-01, G-02, G-03, G-04, G-14, G-17, G-20, G-99, G-136).

| Gap | Current State | Target State | Severity | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|

### 4.1 Counts and the Critical gaps

148 gaps (G-01 to G-148): 24 Critical, 93 Important, 31 Minor (counted from the Severity column of the table above). Critical gaps:

| Gap | Why Critical (rubric) |
|---|---|
| G-01, G-02, G-99 | Finding contract cannot serve every consumer: location types and line grammars cannot flow through one merge and ledger path; closed vocabularies reject PR and rf-qa outright |
| G-03, G-12, G-13, G-14 | Verdict fails open: reviewer-typed blocking, clearing by silence, one valid reviewer of N passes, defer rewrites the verdict |
| G-17 | Two incompatible verdict models and thresholds (0.75 vs 0.80; 3-state vs 4-state) |
| G-11 | Two ledger schemas, one of them installed-only |
| G-20, G-42 | Reflect has two Tier-2 paths that share nothing; the production path is a count-derived, tasklist-only convergence gate |
| G-21, G-84 | C8: panel shipped, reachable only by hand in `shadow`, unreachable from workflow and tasklist |
| G-22, G-137 | C8: registered commands and exported states with no callee or caller |
| G-23 | C8: telemetry store shipped, no automatic writer |
| G-24, G-25 | No dispatch contract for gateway models; served model never recorded; collapse invisible |
| G-36 | No input manifest; the driving document is not delivered by role |
| G-43 | C8: `--fix`, HALTED and deviation machinery enabled by the gate, structurally dormant |
| G-44 | C8 and constraint: executor-class exclusion claimed by docs, not applied |
| G-47 | Shadow steps that are deterministic are performed by the orchestrator LLM; Stage 2 exit fails (13 of 20) |
| G-55 | C8 in effect: citation verification and clustering resolved nothing in 7 of 15 combo runs |
| G-123 | No acceptance-evidence definition; no Tier G evidence exists for any effort |

### 4.2 Rule C8 check: unwired in-scope capabilities

A capability is listed when research files name it as shipped or enabled and show it not wired at its runtime entrypoint. None is downgraded to "future phase": no on-record scope decision deferring any of them is cited in the 18 research files or in the gap rows read (the only deferral text found is the skill's own "ships in Stage 3" statement, which is a staging note, not a recorded decision).

| Capability | Named as | Where it stops | Gap | Treatment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Review panel kernel (#519) | merged, "Stage 0-2" | `--t2-engine panel` rejected, default `legacy`, no consumer passes the flag, quick-depth phases never read it | G-21, G-84 | Critical |
| `superclaude review lint` and `estimate` | registered subcommands (`__init__.py:24-25`) | modules do not exist, import error swallowed | G-22, G-137 | Critical |

### 4.7 Run 1 gap rows

Run 1's gap table is carried with its per-row `Track:` tags. Run 1 counts 145 rows (15 Critical, 66 Important, 64 Minor; V1:760-762) and run 2 counts 148 rows (24 Critical, 93 Important, 31 Minor; V2:1387); both counts were verified and measure different units. Severity ratings differ on facts both reports agree on (Appendix C rows X-011 to X-019). Run 2's rule (V2:1121) and its C8 table (V2:1411-1422) govern the ratings in the base. <!-- Source: new (lead per Change #M-05) -->

**Rule applied to this table (verbatim):** 'Docs may not close a defect (R1-C8, behavioral-reachability control). A gap that is an UNWIRED IN-SCOPE capability — one the driving spec/TDD names as shipped or enabled-by-config but that is NOT actually wired at its runtime entrypoint (no production caller, its result discarded/dead-guarded, or its callee a not-implemented sentinel) — is a DEFECT, not merely future-phase work. It MUST be recorded with Severity Critical/High, MUST carry (or link) an MDTM remediation task under .dev/tasks/to-do/, and MUST NOT be silently downgraded to future phase / later release / Open Question without an on-record, cited scope decision.'

**How the rule is applied in this run.** The run is report-only (owner scope change 2026-11-13). Every row that is an unwired in-scope capability is recorded as Severity Critical, is tagged with the migration track (R1-M1..R1-M4) whose Section 8 steps will wire it (Section 8 is written later by synth-06, which must cover every Critical or Important row of this table), and carries the note `remediation task to be created after the merge of the two reports; none created in this run (owner scope: report only)`. Rows carrying the R1-C8 note: R1-D14, R1-MS-11, R1-MS-14, R1-ENS-1, R1-ENS-3, R1-ENS-4, R1-ENS-5 (restated as doc contradictions R1-DOC-20, R1-DOC-63, R1-DOC-64 and R1-DOC-65 in group (v)). For each, the row cites the document that names the capability as live and the code that shows it unwired; where the research did not establish the "driving spec names it as shipped" premise, the row says so and the point is also carried to Open Questions (Section 9; for R1-D14 this is question R1-Q-58).

**Row groups.** (i) R1-D1..R1-D16, the hand-off defects checked against current code. (ii) BL-nn, blockers for PR code review and for rf-qa / rf-qa-qualitative replacement (each row names the consumers it blocks). (iii) MS-nn, missing shared pieces, consumer hooks and reflect-side gaps. (iv) ENS-nn, the code-driven tasklist post gate (`ensemble.py`). (v) DOC-nn, one row per [CODE-CONTRADICTED] or [STALE DOC] finding (same number as log row `D-nn`). (vi) OPEN-nn, further Important gaps of the log not already carried.
