**Open point for the rf-qa replacement (added at the report-validation gate; the R1-C-18 winner is unchanged).** The decision above assumes "no Bash for reviewers; shell evidence computed by the orchestrator". For rf-qa that assumption is untested: `rf-qa.md` declares Bash (`:10`), calls Read, Grep, Glob and Bash "the primary verification surface" (`:133`) and reports Bash calls in every QA report (`:518`). Classification of its phase checks [proposed, from the text only]: the check lists (research gate 10 items, synthesis gate 12, report validation 19, task integrity 27, fix cycle) are all phrased as Read, Grep or Glob checks, and a search of `rf-qa.md` for `pytest`, `make` and `wc -l` finds only two descriptive mentions (`:327`, `:328`) inside task-integrity checks about what a task file contains, not commands the agent runs; so no listed check is known to need execution, but which checks the agent runs through Bash in practice (test counts, `make` dry-runs, line counts) is not established [UNVERIFIED]. Two ways forward, neither decided here: (a) restrict the replacement to checks that need no execution; (b) give the lens agents a fixed read-only execution tool set for the checks that do, with a test as for `reflect-reviewer` (`test_reviewer_readonly_tools.py:30,78`). The evidence that decides between them is a read-only sample of the `Tool engagement:` lines (Bash counts) in recorded rf-qa reports under past `qa/` directories; until it exists, the "review half only" scope for rf-qa is a hypothesis and the report works on (a) as the default [proposed]. Open item R1-Q-61.

**Adversarial result:** n/a

#### R1-C-19: One verdict contract and exit-code vocabulary (slug: verdict-contract)

This conflict was not on the owner's list; the future-consumer research found several verdict formats that need one owner.

| Effort | Position | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | Four reflect verdicts (PASS, DEGRADED, HALTED, BLOCKED) derived by `derive_verdict`, with exit codes 0/10/11/2 for the wrapper | `contract.py:138-260`; `models.py:39-49`; 05 §1.2, 13 §9.1 [CODE-VERIFIED] |
| E2 | Not studied (round 1 only; deterministic merge printed FAIL or PASS from the ledger) | 02 §4.4 [DOC-SOURCED] |
| E3 | Ledger verdict PASS/FAIL with decision PASS/REVISE/ESCALATE and exit 0/10/11 (`ledger_cmd.py:13`); installed experiment ledger CONTINUE and PENDING with exit 0/10/11/12 (`review_ledger.py:63`); stoprule process codes 0/3/4/5/6 (`stoprule.py:8`); rf-qa and rf-qa-qualitative write `## Overall Verdict: [PASS / FAIL]`; task-builder reads a `VERDICT:` line | 02 §9 item 5; 10 §3 [CODE-VERIFIED] |

##### Option A: the core returns one machine verdict; each module maps it to advisory or blocking and to its native format

**Description:** One verdict and one exit-code set in the core (PASS/REVISE/ESCALATE as today, with an optional PENDING); modules decide gate strength and render their own report line.
**How it works:** `ledger verdict` stays the machine surface; reflect keeps its four-verdict map as a module-side mapping; rf-qa and task-builder lines are generated from the core result.

| Aspect | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Effort | M |
| Risk | Low |
| Reuse of existing code | High |
| Files/systems affected | Core verdict module, consumer skill text, tests that pin exit codes |
| Pros | Verdict ownership in one place; advisory versus blocking stays a module choice (workflow Wave 4 advisory, post gate blocking) |
| Cons | Reflect's contract fields (`tier_reached`, `adversarial_convergence_score`, deviation counts) must stay readable by the gate |

##### Option B: Option A plus rf-qa's monotonicity and regression halts in the core stop rule

**Description:** Also adopt "open blocking count must strictly shrink" and "any PASS to FAIL regression halts" (`rf-qa.md:403-418`).
**How it works:** extra checks in the decision step.

| Aspect | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Effort | M |
| Risk | Medium |
| Reuse of existing code | Medium |
| Files/systems affected | `ledger.py` decision code, rf-qa replacement module |
| Pros | Protects an rf-qa replacement from non-convergence |
| Cons | Untested against the ledger loop; may conflict with the cap-by-refusal rule in R1-C13 |

##### Option C: leave the contracts as they are

**Description:** Three verdict formats and several exit-code sets.
**How it works:** none.

| Aspect | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Effort | XS |
| Risk | Medium |
| Reuse of existing code | Complete |
| Files/systems affected | None |
| Pros | No change |
| Cons | Each new consumer re-invents the mapping; the three formats need "one owner" and have none |

**Evidence:**
- Exit-code vocabularies differ: master `merge` always exits 0, `ledger verdict` exits 0/10/11, the experiment ledger 0/10/11/12 and other process codes, stoprule 0/3/4/5/6 (02 §2, §9 item 5) [CODE-VERIFIED].
- Verdict ownership differs per consumer: spec-panel blocks through the ledger verdict, the tasklist post gate through reflect contract fields, workflow and Stage 10.5 are advisory (09 §8 item 3) [CODE-VERIFIED].
- rf-qa halts on non-monotonic open blocking counts and on regression; the ledger stop rule has neither (`ledger.py:93-104`) (10 §6) [ext][E3] [CODE-VERIFIED]. The benefit of adopting it was not tested.
- Of the 41 review call sites among the 43 rf-* spawning call sites [unit not stated by run 1 and not reproducible by grep: `grep -rEn 'subagent_type: *"?rf-' src/superclaude/skills` gives 52 lines in 11 files, 44 of them in 8 `SKILL.md` files; Appendix E], 32 depend on an in-place fix step that a read-only panel cannot do; the common shape lens, consolidate, one fix agent, verify matches the review loop (10 §3 Key Takeaways) [ext]. <!-- Variant 1 (modified) — M-25 (M-24 item 7): unit note on run 1's 43 call sites -->

**Status:** DECIDED-BY-EVIDENCE: the divergence among at least three formats and four exit-code sets is verified and a single machine verdict with module-side mapping is the only option that keeps the existing consumers working; adopting rf-qa's extra halts is a separate, untested add-on.

**Recommended resolution:** Option A; evaluate Option B's halts on the E2 ground-truth packages before adopting them.

**Adversarial result:** n/a

#### R1-C-20: Rollout and evaluation, shadow mode versus ground-truth benchmark (slug: rollout-evaluation)

This conflict was not on the owner's list; the efforts built two complementary evaluation mechanisms that were never combined.

| Effort | Position | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | Shadow mode: the new path runs beside the authoritative legacy path and writes side artifacts only; an exit script requires 20 runs; it measures non-interference and side signals, "not quality"; Stage 2 exit is FAIL on 2026-11-13 (13 of 20 runs counted; EV-1 rate 8/13 = 0.615 against legacy 3/39 = 0.077; 6 parity and 9 lint or manifest failures); extraction of a generic harness is gated on 20 passing runs and a named second consumer | `shadow-standalone-evaluation.md:47-48,100-132`; `reflect_shadow_exit.py:203-387`; 07 §5; 11 §7 [CODE-VERIFIED for the script and run output; document statements DOC-SOURCED] |
| E2 | Ground truth per package (3 packages, 16 known defects), blind judge over anonymised merged reports, permutation tests, six audits; it measures quality; it has no shadow mechanism or run manifest; the judge is blind to reviewer ids only and never receives `source.md`; `source.md` and raw judge outputs are not committed; many paths live in `/tmp` | E2 `judge-one.sh:12-21`; 11 §2-§4; R1-G-83 [CODE-VERIFIED via `git show`] |
| E3 | Pre-registered screen with fixed limits and an evidence-consistency checker (`final_report_check.py`, no model calls); the bundle reports convergence not proven and no valid-success verdict | FINAL-REPORT.md:42,75,87,250; 11 §11 [DOC-SOURCED, dated 2026-11-08/09] |

##### Option A: shadow mode per consumer only (E1 pattern)

**Description:** Roll out each consumer with its own shadow variant and exit script.
**How it works:** variant runs beside legacy; an aggregator counts clean runs.

| Aspect | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Effort | M per consumer |
| Risk | Medium |
| Reuse of existing code | High |
| Files/systems affected | Per-consumer scripts, `manifest.py` constants pinned by tests |
| Pros | Safe non-interference proof |
| Cons | Measures side signals, never quality; the shadow variant reuses legacy dispatch so it cannot show the panel finds more |

##### Option B: ground-truth benchmark only (E2 pattern)

**Description:** Score panels against known defects with a blind judge.
**How it works:** fixed packages, anonymised outputs, permutation tests.

| Aspect | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Effort | L |
| Risk | Medium |
| Reuse of existing code | Medium: the harness is bash with hard-coded paths, uncommitted inputs and a runner that overwrites attempts |
| Files/systems affected | New portable runner, judge brief with a source slot, committed packages |
| Pros | Measures quality (the only way to compare deciders, R1-C05) |
| Cons | No rollout safety mechanism; three packages and 16 defects only; about 115,000 judge tokens per scoring (document-sourced) |

##### Option C: both, the shadow harness for rollout safety and the ground-truth benchmark as the quality regression set

**Description:** Extract the generic shadow harness (manifest profile plus exit-aggregator skeleton) and port the E2 benchmark behind a portable runner; use both for each consumer.
**How it works:** the exit script is split into a generic aggregator and per-consumer check plugins; the benchmark is hosted where real-`claude` spawning with isolation, timeouts and reporting already exist (`src/superclaude/cli/eval/` is the likely host; this is an inference, not a designed plan).

| Aspect | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Effort | XL |
| Risk | Medium |
| Reuse of existing code | High: extraction plan in `shadow-standalone-evaluation.md:100-123`; `cli/eval` runner |
| Files/systems affected | `manifest.py`, `reflect_shadow_exit.py`, `reflect_verdict_replay.py` (both bound to "1.8.0"), a new benchmark module |
| Pros | Covers both safety and quality; gives R1-C05, R1-C13 and R1-C14 their missing measurements |
| Cons | Largest scope; the benchmark's judge must be made source-aware and fully blind first |

**Evidence:**
- The two harnesses are complementary, not overlapping: E1 has no ground truth and no quality score, E2 has no shadow or authority mechanism and no run manifest (11 §7 assessment) [CODE-VERIFIED reading of both].
- The judge brief carries the combo name (`judge-one.sh:21`) and folder path (`:6`), contradicting the "blind" claim for panel identity (R1-D-55) [E2] [CODE-VERIFIED via `git show`].
- Shadow Stage 2 failures are orchestrator contract-writing and file-placement lapses, not merge quality: three unparseable contracts (`[1m]`), header copied from the harness, `merged-verdict.yaml` at the nested path, extra top-level keys (07 §5.1) [E1] [CODE-VERIFIED]; even the "clean" runs 10, 11, 12 and 14 broke shadow rules in places (R1-G-60).
- No effort can say which model mix finds more real defects for reflect: blind scoring of the 15 combo runs was planned as a separately approved step and was not run (11 §9) [E1].
- The bundle's reusable parts are a fixed pre-registered screen, frozen endpoint hashes and a no-model evidence checker (11 §11 Key Takeaways) [E3].
- External context [web]: the only judge-quality evidence is for answer-correctness scoring; defect-finding panels have no controlled external study, so the project's own labelled packages are the validation set (web-03 §6.5; web-03 Recommendation 4, 7: a bias battery per judge, a judge from a different vendor than every scored reviewer).

**Status:** DECIDED-BY-EVIDENCE: each harness measures what the other cannot and several conflicts above (R1-C05, R1-C13, R1-C14) cannot be resolved without the quality benchmark, so using both is the only option that supplies both safety and measurement; the hosting choice is an inference and is not part of the decision.

**Recommended resolution:** Option C. Treat the shadow harness as the rollout-safety gate and the E2-style benchmark as the quality regression set; first make the benchmark portable (committed `source.md`, source-aware judge brief, panel-blind labels, no `/tmp` paths) and name an owner for the benchmark port (R1-G-59).

**Adversarial result:** n/a

#### R1 6.X Overall design options

These are whole-design options drawn from the SOLUTION_RESEARCH section of the research notes (approaches 1-6). They combine the conflict resolutions above; they are not a roadmap and they do not choose a branch structure. Options A and B are stages of one unification path (A is B's first stage); Option C (keep both stacks) is the only alternative to that path.

```
                 +-----------------------------------------------------------+
 Option B shape: |  shared core                                              |
                 |  finding contract (v2 + lens registry) | panel resolver   |
                 |  dispatcher + adapters | run manifest   | clusterer       |
                 |  citation checks | decider hook | telemetry | verdict     |
                 +--------+----------+-----------+-----------+---------------+
                          |          |           |           |
                    reflect pre/  workflow    spec review   PR code review,
                    post module   tasklist    (brainstorm,  rf-qa replacement
                                  module      design)       (future modules)
```

##### Option A: findings-v2 as the single contract, v1 as a strict subset, on the existing two code stacks

**Description:** Keep the package layout; make findings-v2 the contract that every consumer writes; accept findings-v1 lines as a subset; fix R1-D1..R1-D16 in place; add lenses by editing the closed tuples.
**How it works:** `findings_v2.py` gains the block-level v1 rules the code lacks (empty block, `prior` lines, `reflect-post`) and its docstring is corrected; `LENSES` and the category sets grow by code change; the ledger parses v2; reflect keeps the debate and 1.8.0; the cluster path stays telemetry for reflect.

| Aspect | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Effort | L |
| Risk | Medium |
| Reuse of existing code | High: everything stays; `findings_v2`, `cluster`, `panel`, `manifest`, ledger |
| Files/systems affected | `findings.py`, `findings_v2.py`, `ledger.py`, `merge_cmd.py`, `cluster.py`, briefs, tests that pin v1 text |
| Pros | Smallest path to one contract; E1 and E3 code both survive |
| Cons | Every new lens or category is a code change (`LENSES` and `CATEGORIES` are closed tuples); a code-review or rf-qa finding still needs new severity and location kinds; `merge_round` stays single-document |

##### Option B: a new superset core with pluggable lens and category namespaces and several location types

**Description:** Build the shared core as data-driven registries: lens (candidate kind, severity vocabulary, categories, primary location kind, blocking predicate, id grammar), location union (anchor, citations with role, file and section, multi-file observation with `in_diff`), launch adapters per environment, review kinds beyond first and re-review, and fix and verdict contracts as data; findings-v1 and findings-v2 become profiles of the core.
**How it works:** start from the Option A code (v2 is the natural base, 01 §18), then move the closed tuples into registries; thin modules (reflect pre and post, workflow tasklist, spec review, PR review, rf-qa replacement) declare only their lens, brief slots and gate strength; the core exposes the 13 exposures R1-X1..R1-X13 of research 10 §5.

| Aspect | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Effort | XL |
| Risk | Medium-High |
| Reuse of existing code | High (v2 code, `PROFILES` pattern, reflect profile generalised) but a new registry layer |
| Files/systems affected | the whole `cli/review/` package, reflect skill and templates, `pr_submit` severity router and rubric (one table both sides read), rf-qa agents, telemetry, tier file |
| Pros | Once R1-M1 delivers exposures R1-X1..R1-X14, a new consumer is data plus a thin module (the future-use exposure list; the non-core prerequisites are in the R1-M4 Dependencies); one rule per lens (R1-C16); covers PR location kinds and rf-qa file-and-section locations |
| Cons | Largest design surface; the registry layer is untested; PR and rf-qa seams have open owner choices (finder versus S2b verifier, R1-G-80; rubric versus router authority, R1-G-78) |

##### Option C: keep both stacks and add adapters

**Description:** Do not unify; add `card_convert`-style adapters from each producer to each consumer and share only the panel resolver and the manifest.
**How it works:** document loops keep v1 and the ledger; reflect keeps v2 and the cluster path; PR review and rf-qa get their own adapters.

| Aspect | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Effort | M |
| Risk | Medium |
| Reuse of existing code | Complete |
| Files/systems affected | New adapters only |
| Pros | Fastest; no regression exposure on the 1,182 gate items (12 §8) |
| Cons | The four limits stay in nine places; R1-D1, R1-D5, R1-D9 and the two invalid-block policies remain; every adapter repeats severity-word guesses (rf-qa `IMPORTANT` inverts under `card_convert`); two merge-ledger implementations and a third reflect merge path stay |

**Evidence:**
- The package already holds two stacks with different jobs: v1 decides (findings, ledger, merge, verdict), v2 only flags and records (findings_v2, card_convert, cluster, verify-citations, manifest); v2 imports private v1 names, so v1 edits propagate (research notes PATTERNS; 01 §2) [CODE-VERIFIED].
- Today no consumer exercises the E1 kernel in production and the #346 merge and ledger CLI has exactly one in-repo caller (09 §5, §7) [CODE-VERIFIED]; migrating consumers is therefore not blocked by existing production callers except the tasklist post gate through `ensemble.py` (R1-C17).
- The core would have to expose open lenses, per-lens categories and severities, a location union, multi-artifact candidates with a pluggable clustering key, roles separate from models, more review kinds, fix and verdict contracts as data, provenance for grading, and model-role mapping and strata as data (10 §5 R1-X1..R1-X13) [CODE-VERIFIED reading]; today's closed `LENSES`, spec-only `CATEGORIES`, three-level severity, single-document anchor clustering, model-only templates, `--kind first|re-review` and sonnet/haiku strata each block at least one future consumer (10 §6).
- Reflect's frozen contract 1.8.0 permits sharing resolution, cards, clustering, citation checks, calibration coverage and manifests, but not the merge decision or contract writer (07 §10 Q8) [CODE-VERIFIED].
- External context [web]: production AI review systems separate finders from a coordinator that deduplicates, verifies against source and applies a severity rubric, and dedup on typed location and category rather than text similarity (https://blog.cloudflare.com/ai-code-review; web-04 R1-D1, R1-D2); SARIF models location as a union of physical, logical and snippet-hash kinds (web-04 R1).

**Assessment summary:** Options A and B are two stages of one unification path (B starts from A's code, so A is B's first stage), and Option C is the only real alternative to that path and the only choice that leaves the measured defect classes unchanged; the comparison is therefore between "unify, in stages" and "do not unify", not three independent designs. The conflict resolutions above are consistent with building toward Option B through Option A. Decided by evidence: R1-C01, R1-C02, R1-C04, R1-C06 to R1-C12, R1-C15 to R1-C20. Resolved by adversarial debate and left `partial`: R1-C03, R1-C05, R1-C13 and R1-C14. Option B depends on those four: the launch adapters and the class-launch grammar on R1-C03 (owner item R1-O-2, the target environment), the decider the registry carries on R1-C05, the ledger rounds model on R1-C13, and the template and reviewer-count defaults on R1-C14 (Decision R1-D-1).

#### Options Comparison

| Criterion | Option A: findings-v2 single contract, v1 subset | Option B: new superset core, pluggable lenses and location types | Option C: keep both stacks with adapters |
|---|---|---|---|
| Effort | L | XL | M |
| Risk | Medium | Medium-High (new registry layer, wider blast radius) | Medium (drift grows) |
| Maintainability | Good for existing lenses; every new lens is a code change in closed tuples | Best long term: lenses, categories, severities and predicates are data; one validator | Poor: limits and rules duplicated in nine places; two ledger paths and a third reflect merge path stay |
| Integration complexity | Medium: v1 consumers move to v2 parsing; ledger gains citations | High: touches package, skills, PR router, rf-qa agents, telemetry | Low per adapter, rising with each consumer |
| Reuse potential | High for reflect and document loops; low for PR and rf-qa without new kinds | High for all consumers by design (R1-X1..R1-X13) | Low: each consumer gets its own mapping |
| Future-consumer fit: PR code review | Weak: needs `in_diff`, five-tier severity, `line: null`, multi-file observations, closed PR reviewer set | Strong: location union and per-lens severity and predicate; seam choice (finder or S2b verifier) still open | Weak to medium: adapter can map fields but not the severity and merge semantics |
| Future-consumer fit: rf-qa replacement | Weak: `file:section` locations, IMPORTANT-as-blocking and fix-agent hand-off are missing | Strong for the review half; the 32 call sites that need an in-place fix keep a separate fix agent (Reviser) | Weak: severity words invert under today's word map |

**Condition on the Option B ratings.** The Medium-High risk of Option B is conditional: it holds only if the four debate-gated conflicts (R1-C-03, R1-C-05, R1-C-13, R1-C-14) are settled, and they ended `partial` with 26 unaddressed HIGH invariants in total (2 + 11 + 10 + 3, each debate's own numbering), and it assumes owners for two things nobody has named: approval of changes to the shared core (R1-O-4, R1-G-92) and the benchmark port (R1-G-59). With those open the risk is higher than the table reads. The effort and risk lines of the single conflicts in Section 6 are pre-debate ratings; the "Rating of the adopted resolution" lines of R1-C-03, R1-C-05, R1-C-11 and R1-C-14 give the adopted ones.

**Recommended design (not a roadmap):** build toward Option B through Option A's code. Start from findings-v2 as the single contract (R1-C01), keep the debate and contract 1.8.0 for reflect (R1-C11), and move the closed tuples into lens registries as new consumers need them. Option C is rejected because it leaves R1-D1, R1-D5, R1-D9, the opposite invalid-block policies and the third merge path in place.

## 7. Recommendation

*Source note carried from the preamble of `synthesis/synth-07-recommendation-architecture.md`:*

Source: research files 01 to 18 in `.dev/tasks/to-do/TASK-RESEARCH-review-panel-run2-20261114-075454/research/`, and, for the adjudication fold (item 5.50), the 15 `ADJUDICATION-RESULT.md` files under `reviews/adversarial/<slug>/` of the same task folder (one per undecidable conflict slot of synth-06 6.12.9; X-13, X-14 and X-15 are the synth-06 slots C-13, C-14 and C-15). All 15 debates were adjudicated, at depth `standard`, each with return-contract status `partial`.

Citation form: `rNN §x` = research file `NN-*.md`, section x. `HEAD` = commit 50d4d2b9d on `ironbelly/shadow-runs`; `E2 tip` = 6c0984326cbb8fb06c4a36065de58b171d3f8175. Evidence tags follow the research files: [CODE-VERIFIED], [CODE-CONTRADICTED], [UNVERIFIED]. Only [CODE-VERIFIED] statements carry the recommendation; [CODE-CONTRADICTED] statements appear in their corrected form; [UNVERIFIED] statements are flagged where they appear and collected in the closing list for the Open Questions section. Design statements are marked [DESIGN] and are inferences from verified facts, not facts.

E1 = reflect Tier 2 kernel, shadow mode and the model-combination experiment. E2 = tasklist review-panel study, collaboration and process-redesign designs (no product code at any commit: r01 §1.1). E3 = the #346 review loop: E3s = shipped source (`src/superclaude/cli/review` v1 path, `src/superclaude/commands/spec-panel.md` Review Loop, `src/superclaude/rules/prompts/document_review_loop_prompts.md`); E3i = installed-only variants under `~/.claude` (r01 §4.1).


**Recommended approach:** **One Shared Review Panel Core: a Thin Shared Contract with Per-Module Engines.** (This design was named "One Review Panel Core with Module Profiles" before the adjudication fold; it is renamed because debate C-01 overturned the default that the v2 kernel is the single engine of the core. See 7.0.1.) One shared Review Panel core lives in the existing package `src/superclaude/cli/review/` and is reached by installed skills and commands only through the `superclaude review ...` CLI. What the core shares across every module is a thin contract: the finding id grammar (`_ID`), one limits-constants module and one repair step that both parsers call, one reference-token list (with `T<PP>.<TT>` added once), hash and identity helpers, panel and tier resolution from one reviewed tier file, the run record (per-run events, a manifest lock, a cross-run telemetry export), the dispatch contract (the core launches nothing; a reviewer is launched with its `launch` word) and a tested evaluation script set. What it does not share is one engine: the spec-review module keeps the v1 anchor parser, `findings.py`, `ledger.py`, `review-ledger/1` and v1 clustering, with the clearing and merge-policy rules of C-02 and C-03; reflect and later PR review use the v2 kernel (`findings_v2.py`, `cluster.py`, citations with role, path and lines), and the v2 kernel is NOT the engine of the spec loop. Every consumer (reflect, tasklist and workflow review through reflect UC-1, spec review for `sc:spec-panel` and later `sc:brainstorm` and `sc:design`, and later PR code review and rf-qa / rf-qa-qualitative replacement) is a thin module made of profile data (vocabularies, label maps, reference patterns, lens and role tables, cap), brief blocks, and an output adapter. The reflect module keeps contract 1.8.0, the pure `contract.derive_verdict` shell, its 36-test matrix and, for now, engine A's ensemble as the production Tier 2 engine; the panel enters reflect only behind the reflect call (C-04, C-05). No consumer copies core text; the brief limits, categories and constants are generated from the core. Convergence to one engine is a recorded later path with three triggers (T-a, T-b, T-c: 7.0.1), not the starting point.

### 7.0.1 Name, owner wording and how the 15 outcomes combine

Name and owner wording. The owner approved the wording "one shared Review Panel core in `src/superclaude/cli/review/`, with thin modules for reflect, tasklist and workflow, spec review, and later PR review". The adjudicated design is describable in those terms in two respects: there is one shared core location (the package `cli/review/`, where both engines already live) and the consumers are thin modules. It differs in one respect, flagged here and in the fold report: the core is a shared contract plus two engines that sit side by side in the package, not one engine on which every module is a profile (the spec loop stays on the v1 engine, reflect and PR review on the v2 kernel; debate C-01, `reviews/adversarial/core-shape-and-finding-contract/`). The earlier name implied a single engine and is retired; the owner is asked to confirm the new reading (synth-10 Q-40).

Precedence. Section 3 (target elements T-1 to T-6, the 3.2 table, the success criteria SC-01 to SC-33, 3.5) and the Target State cells of Section 4 were written before the adjudication fold. Where they differ from 7.0, 7.0.1 or 7.1, this section governs; the delta table at the head of Section 3 lists the items concerned and the outcome that replaces each.

How the 15 outcomes combine into one design (every row is the outcome of the debate named; folder paths are in the choices table after the axes table):

| Debate (slot) | What it adds to the one design | Where it lands in 7.1 |
|---|---|---|
| C-01 core shape | Thin shared contract now; per-module engines (spec = v1, reflect and PR = v2); open unknown keys; `prior` lines unchanged; anchor status shown in the per-row `### Lx` block; one engine only if T-a, T-b or T-c fires | Elements 1, 2, 3, 5 |
| C-06 limits repair | One repair step inside both `parse_block` functions behind `repair=False`: cut of `anchor`, `anchor2` and citation `quote` to 200 flattened characters, itemised drop record, dropped-blocking refusal, one re-ask; claim cut unresolved | Element 1 |
| C-02 ledger clearing | In the v1 engine: quorum-gated explicit clearing, silence never clears, typed `blocking` plus CRITICAL floor, `defer` terminal and counted open, verdict derived on read | Elements 4, 5 |
| C-03 merge policy | In the v1 engine: any-blocking union (pluggable policy), quorum as a merge-time refusal (floor `min(2, requested)`), no calibrator in the default; fail-closed only in profiles that set `degrade`; reflect keeps `shortfall: visible` | Element 4 |
| C-09 tier source | One reviewed tier file held in step with the env slot lists by one guard; soft distinctness default; scarcest-first order in the CLI; `requested_slots` and `distinct_models` always written | Element 6 |
| C-07 dispatch | The core launches nothing; Agent class word shipped; raw-id `claude -p` launcher gated (G1-G3); no packaged gateway fill | Element 6 |
| C-08 run record | Per-run `events.jsonl`, transcript adapter gated by M1, manifest lock, `review-telemetry/1` with `strict`, identity gate in the exit script | Element 8 |
| C-04 reflect engine | No engine moves now; engine A stays production Tier 2; code-owned write-side helpers as comparison siblings; D1 fixes now; single-engine decision named, not scheduled | Reflect module, element 6 |
| C-05 consumer entry | Reflect UC-1 stays the only tasklist and workflow entry; advisory at Wave 4, "advisory-blocking" at Stage 10.5, blocking at T5; no plugin copy | Tasklist and workflow module |
| X-15 (C-15) tasklist Medium | Label map as module data; fidelity prompt outside the core; whether Medium blocks is unresolved (H+ versus A+) | Tasklist module |
| C-10 PR wire format | Separate pre-step, pure converter on the `pr_submit` side, sibling `panel` field, report-only first release | PR module |
| C-11 rf-qa first step | Lens-level first change: one new read-only lens agent and a replay oracle; no panel engine in any rf-qa gate | rf-qa module |
| C-12 collaboration | H1, H2, H3, H4 principle and the static kit (`kit: off`) now; exchange not built; triggers | Elements 1, 7 |
| X-13 (C-13) process redesign | Optional card format, row block, advisory rowcheck, dormant until a module declares cards; no demotion or promotion | Elements 3, 7 |
| X-14 (C-14) evaluation | Three-tier acceptance, metric of record, tested script set; kernel `verify-run` deferred | Element 9 |

Where two outcomes pull against each other, the combination the results themselves support is stated here and the tension is an open question (synth-10 section 9.10), never a silent choice:

| # | Outcomes in tension | Combination the results support | Open question |
|---|---|---|---|
| CT-1 | C-01 (thin contract, "no change to `cli/reflect`") against C-12 (H1 needs a reflect brief edit at `cli/reflect/ensemble.py:601-630`) and C-04 (write-side helpers, placement open) | "No change to `cli/reflect`" is read as additive files only (C-04); the H1 edit and the helper placement are not covered by that reading | Q-41 |
| CT-2 | C-01 (a repair step inside both parsers, all pins unmodified) against C-06 (`repair=False` keyword; v1 merge keeps the cut) | The repair is reachable only through the keyword, so a default parse keeps the pins at `test_review_findings.py:113,117`; whether v1 `merge` may pass `repair=True` is not shown | Q-43 |
| CT-3 | C-02 (need = `min(Q, requested)`), C-03 (floor `min(2, requested)`), C-06 (which blocks count as eligible) and C-09 (the spec loop does not pass the resolution to merge) | One `requested` count per round is needed by all four; none of the four debates fixes where it comes from when `--resolution` is absent | Q-42 |
| CT-4 | X-14 (identity check reports `unrecorded` until a writer exists) against C-08 (the writer is gated by M1, measured 0 of 15 on the usage clause) | Tier S cannot read `pass` for identity until C-08's M1 passes; "accepted" stays unreachable until then | Q-44 |
| CT-5 | X-15 (H+ keeps MAJOR non-blocking rows droppable) against C-02 (CRITICAL floor only) | Under H+ a dropped-criterion class typed MAJOR with `blocking: false` is not floored | Q-45 |
| CT-6 | C-07 (class-word dispatch only ships) against C-09 (distinct gateway panels are distinct requested ids) | Diversity is recorded as requested, not served, until C-08's M1 passes; `--env gateway` still refuses without an explicit tier file | Q-46 |

The design stays ONE coherent design under these tensions because each is a question about a parameter, a placement or a gate, not about which engine owns which module.

Verified facts that bound the design to ONE shape. They rule out the E3i scripts, reflect engine A and the E2 harness scripts as a base; the choice among the v2 kernel, the v1 package and a thin shared contract as the core (axis 1) was decided by debate C-01 in favour of the thin shared contract with per-module engines:

| # | Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| F-1 | The `cli/review` kernel is the one engine E1 and E3s already share; E1 is a strict superset of E3s for panel resolution and the line grammar | r01 §4.2 row 8, §4.3 row 8 [CODE-VERIFIED] |
| F-2 | The package exists (25 tracked files, optional-module registration through `review_group`) and imports nothing from `cli/reflect`; `cli/reflect` imports nothing from `cli/review` | r18 §6.1, §9 [CODE-VERIFIED] |
| F-3 | E2 changed no file under `src/` or `tests/` on its whole branch; it contributes data, requirements, designs and harness scripts | r01 §1.1 [CODE-VERIFIED] |
| F-4 | E3i (`review_ledger.py`, `stoprule.py`, `diffgate.py`, `fix_audit.py`, 7,589 lines) is stdlib-only, imports nothing from the package, is not in `src/`, and is not touched by `superclaude install` | r03 §3.1, r14 §3.2 [CODE-VERIFIED] |
| F-5 | In production `superclaude reflect run` uses the swarm ensemble (engine A), whose reviewers see the tasklist body only, which emits contract `1.0`, and which has no calibrator, evidence validator or deviation classes; the skill panel (engine B) has all of those and the 1.8.0 contract | r06 §2, §4.1, §5, §7 [CODE-VERIFIED] |
| F-6 | The defects that decide verdicts (clearing by silence, one valid reviewer passes, stored verdict, whole-line drops) sit in the kernel and are pinned by tests as intended behaviour | r03 §1, §2; r17 final register [CODE-VERIFIED] |

### Rationale: the 11 decision axes

For each axis: the options found in the evidence, what is chosen, why, and the trade-off accepted. Axes whose choice depended on a conflict the evidence could not decide were adjudicated by debate (`reviews/adversarial/<slug>/`); their "Chosen" cell names the debate result, and the table that follows this table gives, per choice, the winner, its conditions and the debate folder. Where a debate overturned the earlier default (axes 1, 2, 4, 5, 8), the cell says so.

### 7.1 Target Architecture

Shared core and thin modules. The core is one package reached through one CLI. It holds a thin shared contract (ids, limits, repair, references, hashes, panel and tier resolution, run record, brief hooks, evaluation hooks) and two engines that sit side by side (the v1 anchor engine used by the spec-review module and the v2 citation kernel used by reflect and PR review); modules are profile data, brief blocks and adapters; consumers are the installed skills and commands that exist today plus the later ones. The outcomes of debates C-01 to X-15 are folded into the diagram and the tables below; the paths of the debate folders are in the choices table of 7.0 and in synth-06 6.12.9.1.

### 7.2 Future-Use Exposure Check

Test applied to every candidate (derived in r13 §9 from the verified code): (1) reviewers are read-only, (2) findings carry file:line or citation locations, (3) severity, category and lens are declared by the module, (4) revision is a separate role, (5) the cap is declared by the module, (6) outward actions stay outside the core. The minimum exposures r13 §8 names (M1-M14) map onto the core elements of 7.1 as follows: M1 locator = met by engine separation (the v2 engine carries citations; no locator-agnostic `annotate` or citation-keyed ledger row after debate C-01) and by the PR converter that reads the citation line (C-10); M2 module-declared sets = element 1; M3 passthrough fields (`in_diff`, `confidence`, `original_line`, `reviewer`) = not core fields after C-10: the PR converter computes `in_diff` and sets `reviewer` by code and leaves `confidence` and `original_line` unset; M4 per-slot lens = withdrawn from the first rf-qa change (C-11), reserved in element 6; M5 read-only reviewer contract = element 6 and 7; M6 reviser as separate role = element 5; M7 cap, blocking rule and severity-to-route as module parameters = elements 4 and 5; M8 one "reviewer failed" finding and the regression / monotonicity guards as pure functions = element 4 and 5; M9 optional checklist output mode = element 4; M10 purity = invariant I-7; M11 output adapter = element 1; M12 main-session invocation rule = element 6; M13 behavioural fixture = element 9; M14 shipping form = invariant I-9.

**Verdict, PR code review: the final shape does NOT block it (NO).** Condition: the v2 engine's citations, module-declared category / lens / severity sets (the FX-5 category parameters on `check_finding`; without them the use is blocked at the closed-category row) and a pure converter on the `pr_submit` side must be in the shape; the first release is report-only, so passthrough fields and a multi-file ledger target are not conditions of it. A later revise loop over citation-located findings is blocked by the v1 ledger until a C-01 trigger (T-a) fires. A second condition: the PR module reviews untrusted diffs, so every launch lane it uses must keep reviewers read-only at process or tool level; a raw-id `claude -p` lane without a process-level tool restriction (not read-only by construction: synth-05 6.5 option 2; r13 R1) is not offered to it.

**Verdict, rf-qa / rf-qa-qualitative replacement: the final shape does NOT block it (NO).** Condition: the reviewers are read-only at process or tool level on every launch lane this module uses. The Agent lane is read-only through the agent definition; the raw-id `claude -p` lane is not read-only by construction (E2's launcher disallows only `Edit Write NotebookEdit` and leaves Bash open), so it is excluded for this module unless it is launched with a process-level tool restriction (synth-05 6.5 option 2; r13 R1). The `/task` phase gate is the one place that already separates read-only lens agents from one fix agent (`task/SKILL.md:225-256`), so the lens and reviser interfaces above fit it without new Python; the adjudicated first change (debate C-11) is lens-level: one new read-only lens-reviewer agent and a replay oracle, no panel engine in any rf-qa gate, a conditional switch at `/task` steps 3-4. The checklist mode, the document-type packs and any panel engine behind a gate (which waits for the anchor probe, the C-03 floor owner and C-02's caller rules) are what a full replacement still needs.

### 7.4 Run 1 recommendation and architecture (recorded alternative)

Run 2's adjudicated recommendation governs; this block is run 1's recommendation, kept as the recorded one-engine alternative and for its exposure list and blockers table, which run 2 does not have in this form. The V1 advocate holds that the core-shape difference is a label (MERGE/BOTH); the V2 advocate holds V2 (C-076, unresolved). Ordering words in this block are run 1's recommendation, not an order of work in this document. <!-- Source: new (lead per Change #M-11) -->

**Known-contradicted claims not built on** (as in synth-04): the experiment variants exist only in the bundle (they are also installed in `~/.claude/`); audits B, C, E and F have summaries; "4 verdicts flipped" (audit D names 3); "alias GT3 found once" (it is alias GT1, B6); the hand-off's line numbers for R1-D7, R1-D11 and R1-D12; the `ledger.merge_round` docstring on clearing (`ledger.py:112`; the code at `:254-258` never reads `block_ok`).

**One figure corrected here.** Older wording ("35 of 39 Tier 2 runs were driven by the parsed-sparse format flag", synth-04 Option B pros of R1-C-14 and the earlier `research/11` wording) is not used. The R1-C14 debate recount (`reviews/adversarial/panel-size-cost/adversarial/return-contract.yaml`, `escalation_figure_after_check`) is: the parsed-sparse flag was set in 35 of 39 recorded non-shadow runs (34 of the 38 Tier 2 runs) and was decisive in 0 for certain and at most 1 of 39; 29 of the 34 flagged Tier 2 runs also have a recorded escalate row 4, 5 or 6. [E1] [CODE-VERIFIED in data by the debate's own script `recount_tier_decision.py`; the full command, input glob and key mapping are in the R1-C-14 Evidence block, Section 6; counts only]

**Recommended approach:** Option B from 6.X Overall design options (a new superset core with pluggable lens, category and location namespaces, and thin per-consumer modules), built *through* Option A's code: findings-v2 becomes the single contract with findings-v1 accepted as a strict subset (R1-C-01), and the closed tuples (`LENSES`, `CATEGORIES`, severity words, `_KINDS`, `STRATA`) move into data registries only as each consumer needs them. Option C (keep both stacks and add adapters) is rejected. This is exactly the "Recommended design (not a roadmap)" of synth-04 6.X; nothing below overrides it.

**Rationale:**

1. **The Options Comparison favours B for the two consumers that matter after the first ones.** On the Options Comparison criteria B is XL effort and Medium-High risk but the only option that is "Strong" for both PR code review and the rf-qa replacement (A is "Weak", C "Weak to medium"), because the future consumers need open lenses, per-lens categories and severities, a location union, multi-artifact candidates, roles separate from models and fix/verdict contracts as data (R1-X1..R1-X13, `research/10` section 5). Option A alone leaves every new lens a code change in closed tuples (R1-C-01 Cons; `findings_v2.py:36`, `findings.py:15-22`). Option C leaves R1-D1, R1-D5, R1-D9, the two opposite invalid-block policies and the third reflect merge path (`ensemble.py`) in place and repeats the severity-word guesses that already invert rf-qa `IMPORTANT` under `card_convert` (`card_convert.py:71-83`).
2. **A is B's first stage, so the order costs nothing.** B starts from A's code (v2 is the natural base, `research/01` section 18; `PROFILES` and `PRIMARY_ROLES` are the registry precedents, `review_ledger.py:53-59` [E3-installed], `cluster.py:67-70` [E1]). B depends on the four debate-resolved (`partial`) conflicts in these places: its launch adapters and class-launch grammar depend on R1-C-03 (owner item R1-O-2, the target environment), the decider on R1-C-05, the round model on R1-C-13, and the template and reviewer-count defaults on R1-C-14 (Decision R1-D-1). The architecture below leaves all four as declared hooks or owner-gated items, not as built behaviour.
3. **What the core owns and what stays per module follows the reflect contract.** Contract 1.8.0, `panel_lint` and the wrapper allow the core to own resolution, cards, clustering, citation checks, calibration coverage and manifests (all telemetry today), but not reflect's merge decision or contract writer without a bump (`research/07` Q8; R1-C-11). Hence "verdict computed in the core, advisory-or-blocking policy and report format in each module" (R1-C-19) and "the debate stays reflect's decider" (R1-C-11).
4. **Decided conflicts are built as written; the four debate-resolved ones are staged behind hooks, gates or owner items.** Sixteen of the twenty conflicts are DECIDED-BY-EVIDENCE (R1-C-01, R1-C-02, R1-C-04, R1-C-06 to R1-C-12, R1-C-15 to R1-C-20); their resolutions are adopted as written (within R1-C-04, only the per-slot distinctness policy and no silent re-admission are decided; `replicas` is a design option). R1-C-03, R1-C-05, R1-C-13 and R1-C-14 were resolved by adversarial debate and every one ended `partial` (convergence blocked by unaddressed HIGH invariants); the architecture is not independent of them (Rationale 2). They are carried as open design risks in the table below, not as solved questions.
5. **Measured evidence is thin on quality everywhere, so the design buys measurement.** The only decider measured against ground truth is the single-reviewer veto, and that evidence is negative on precision (65 judge-blocking against 38 real; +2.75 to 3.25 wrong blockers when doubling two models) [E2] [DOC-SOURCED]; the grader, quorum, calibrator and debate have no accuracy data (R1-C-05); 2 versus 3 reflect reviewers, Tier 2 versus Tier 1 recall (R1-H-A) and rounds 2-3 under a multi-reviewer ledger were never measured (R1-C-13, R1-C-14). The architecture therefore keeps the veto live, records the grader and shadow signals beside it, and makes the shadow harness plus a portable E2-style benchmark part of the core (R1-C-20) so the gates can be passed with data.
6. **Default panel size.** The reflect Tier 2 default stays at three reviewers with the hard cap of 3 (`_REFLECT_MAX_REVIEWERS = 3`, `panel.py:73`); the R1-C-14 merge (Option B as merged, `reviews/adversarial/panel-size-cost/proposal-merged.md`) first records the escalation rows and the calibrated confidence at decision time (Step A: audit-only keys `matching_rows`, `calibrated_C_t1`, `S_domains_basis`, `tier_without_flag`, `sparse_flag_decisive`, `escalation_path` in `tier_decision.yaml`, and telemetry `reviewers_requested`, `reviewers_resolved`, `reviewers_source`); the parsed-sparse pre-filter (`SKILL.md:284,443`) stays unchanged unless those keys show it decisive (Conditional item R1-CI-1, because the flag was decisive in 0 for certain and at most 1 of 39 runs); the cap stays 3; the count is decided after R1-H-A on a symmetric pre-registered rule (Step C: three pinned arms, Tier 1, Tier 2 with two reviewers, Tier 2 with three) with Decision R1-D-1 owner-gated (Step B). A skill-path default of two reviewers (9 of 38 recorded Tier 2 runs already ran two cards) is carried only as the owner-gated Decision R1-D-1 of the R1-C-14 merge; this report does not take it. Packaged template defaults (default 4 reviewers, `live7` 7, `review-panel.default.json:9-11`, `review-panel.live7.json:9-13`) are not changed by this recommendation (owner decision 6 of the R1-C-14 merge: blocked on R1-C-03).
7. **Cost trade-offs the owner must see.** B is the largest design surface; its registry layer is untested; the PR and rf-qa seams have open owner choices (finder versus S2b verifier, R1-G-80; rubric versus router authority, R1-G-78). The all-reviewer source injection of R1-C-10 multiplies source tokens by the reviewer count and its cost was never measured (R1-G-47); it interacts with R1-D-1. The grader (R1-C-05) is class-disjoint from the reviewers by design (a design note: the proposed grader is not code and has no `calibrator_diversity` field); in the anthropic-only cell that R1-C-03 selects the class-disjoint set is empty only with the three-reviewer default (sonnet, haiku, opus), and with `--reviewers 2` opus stays free (`research/05` section 12; `reflection-rubric.md:153`; R1-C-06 Cons).

| Severity interchange | SARIF `level` has three buckets and `rank` is the lossless order; native value kept under its native name | https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/sarif-v2.1.0.html | official standard (web-02) |
| Finding identity | CodeQL `primaryLocationLineHash` covers a fixed 100-character normalised window; complete-link, centre-based assignment and size caps are the documented remedies for chaining | https://github.com/github/codeql-action/blob/main/src/fingerprints.ts ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4849582 | official source and papers in another domain (web-04) |
| Judge calibration | verbalized numeric confidence is overconfident and top-skewed; no controlled external study of heterogeneous panels for defect finding or specification review exists, so the project's own labelled packages are the validation set | https://arxiv.org/html/2611.01829v1 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22548 | preprints (web-03 section 6.5) |

#### R1 7.1 Target architecture (d)

**Status of this section.** It is a target derived from the research design inputs (`research/01` §18, `02` §9, `03` Q9, `04` §10, `06` §6, `08` §11.3, `09` §8, `10` §5) and the conflict resolutions above. No research file shows it implemented; every box exists today only as separate E1, E2 or E3 pieces, and names marked [proposed] do not exist in code. "Built from" says which effort and file already supplies the piece.

##### R1 7.1.1 Layers: one shared core, thin per-use-case modules

```
 thin modules: each declares only data (lens, severity words, categories, primary location
 kind, id grammar, blocking predicate, brief slots, rubric, gate strength, output format)
 +---------------+ +----------------+ +-----------------+ +------------+ +----------------+
 | sc:reflect    | | sc:workflow /  | | spec review:    | | PR code    | | rf-qa /        |
 | UC-1 shadow   | | sc:tasklist    | | brainstorm,     | | review     | | rf-qa-qual.    |
 | then panel,   | | tasklist       | | design, spec-   | | (M4,       | | replacement    |
 | UC-2 (M2)     | | review (M3)    | | panel loop (M3) | | finder or  | | (M4, review    |
 |               | |                | |                 | | verifier)  | | half only)     |
 +-------+-------+ +-------+--------+ +--------+--------+ +-----+------+ +--------+-------+
         |                 |                   |                |                 |
 ========v=================v===================v================v=================v========
  SHARED CORE  src/superclaude/cli/review/  (M1)      CLI: superclaude review <subcommand>
  +---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | lens registry (data): severity words, categories, location kind, id grammar, predicate|
  | finding contract (findings-v2 superset; v1 strict subset; per-line rejection record)  |
  | panel resolver (templates, tiers, roles, distinctness, opt. replicas, launch grammar) |
  | identity triple + dispatcher (pin audited, adapters)  | brief renderer ({{SOURCE}}..) |
  | run manifest (profile-declared stages, attempt payloads) -> telemetry projection      |
  | clusterer (one location model) | citation checks (no model call)                     |
  | calibrator (optional)          | decider hook: live veto, shadow blind grader         |
  | round model (ledger)           | merge + verdict (one machine verdict)                |
  | run-audit check interface (manifest-derived checks, before `published`) | shadow    |
  | harness + portable benchmark hook                                                     |
  +---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  reflect module side (not core): 1.8.0 contract writer, EV-1, panel_lint, verdict replay
  fix agents (Reviser, rf-qa fix agent, /sc:troubleshoot) stay OUTSIDE the core: the core
  hands off consolidated blocking findings; reviewers are read-only (allowlist) everywhere
```

##### R1 7.1.2 Data flow for one run (target)

```
 module            core step                                              evidence it rests on
 ------            ---------                                              --------------------
 declares lens --> 1 panel resolve --template @x --run-id --kind          pure, sha256-frozen (panel.py)
                   2 manifest init/advance: frozen inputs, launch_binding  manifest.py, C-03 merge
                   3 brief render: Task, Inputs, Grounding hunks, Lens,    C-10; hunks computed by the
                     Output contract (limits from one constant)            orchestrator (C-18)
                   4 dispatch: one read-only reviewer per slot, Agent      C-09; reflect-reviewer.md:5-8
                     call carries model = launch; served model observed    extract.py:56-58 (offline today)
                     where the adapter can
                   5 collect: parse findings block per reviewer; keep      C-02, C-15
                     valid lines, truncate-and-count, reviewer `partial`,
                     persist rejected_lines
                   6 cluster (v2 location model, complete-link) +          C-12; verify_cmd.py
                     verify-citations (no model call)
                   7 candidates -> decider hook: live hardened veto,       C-05 (shadow grader), C-16
                     shadow blind grader; per-lens predicate sets          (predicate in data)
                     blocking_effective
                   8 round model: round 1 finds; later rounds verify-only  C-13 (staged; gate not passed)
                   9 verdict: PASS / REVISE / ESCALATE + degraded marker   C-19, ledger_cmd.py:13
 maps verdict  <-- 10 built-in audits before `published`; telemetry as a   C-07; reflect_shadow_exit.py
 to advisory or       projection of the committed manifest
 blocking + its
 own report format
```

##### R1 7.1.4 Thin modules

A thin module owns only what differs per consumer: its lens declaration (data), brief slot values, id grammar, blocking predicate, rubric (if a grader applies), gate strength and output rendering. It calls the core through `superclaude review ...` plus one shared brief-and-dispatch reference (the CLI alone briefs and dispatches nothing today, `research/09` §8 item 1). Verdict computation stays in the core; advisory versus blocking is a module choice (R1-C-19).

Exposure ids R1-X1..R1-X13 are those of `research/10` section 5 (R1-X14 is added here, marked [proposed]); BL-nn are the matching gap rows of synth-02. Form names marked [proposed] are not in code; every "Today's blocker" cite is code-verified in the research file named.

#### 8.1.1 Rules applied, and how the three carried Gate 1 findings were resolved

Rules. (1) Rows were processed one ledger at a time and written to this file ledger by ledger; no row text was re-typed from memory. The assignment asked for appends by Edit in chunks of about 40 rows; 5,950 rows with about 1.9 MB of statements cannot be re-typed without error, so each append was made by a read-only script that read the rows of one ledger (Statement, Source, Kind and the ledger Reason are copied byte for byte) and appended them under their destination heading; the script is a tool, not a summary, and it is not part of the deliverable. (2) Each row has exactly one destination, taken from the row's own ledger destination (or, for a register row, the first word of its Fix owner cell) unless a rule below changed it; every change is written in the row's Reason column. (3) Only [CODE-VERIFIED] claims are stated as fact; [UNVERIFIED] and [CODE-CONTRADICTED] tags stay inside the Statement and Reason text as the ledgers wrote them. (4) Report only: no roadmap, branch plan, PR plan or risk register. (5) The run-1 task folder and the queued-run note that the task rules exclude were not read, listed, searched or cited, and `.dev/tasks/` was excluded from every repo-wide search; the one input outside the research files is the Gate 1 consolidated findings file `qa/qa-consolidated-findings-phase3.md` (table 1b), which the owner decision of 2026-11-14 named as additional input.

Which column is authoritative (P3-012, stated once). The defect register and the value ledgers measure different things (who fixes the defect versus where the value goes), and the register carries a reproduction status per row. Rule used for every defect that appears in both: if the register row was re-verified (Repro column REPRODUCED, TRACED or partly TRACED) the register's Fix owner is the destination of the kept row, and each ledger row of the same defect becomes `DROP: duplicate of DR-nnn`; if the register row is UNVERIFIED the ledger destination is kept and the register row becomes `DROP: duplicate of VL-NN-nnn` (it keeps its Fix owner text in the Reason column). A ledger row that was already DROP stays DROP and gets a note `same defect as DR-nnn (kept row)`. The register's first-word rule for dual-owner cells is used (for example `HARNESS / CORE` is HARNESS, `OPS` rows were both UNVERIFIED and resolved against their ledger twin). DR-167 (verified, owner EVAL, an untracked checkout) is DROP because cleaning it is a mutation outside a report-only task. Result: 162 register rows have at least one ledger twin (208 register/ledger pairs); in 99 of those pairs the two destinations differed before this pass (the Gate 1 reviewer found 51 as a lower bound); after it each defect of the listed pairs has one kept row. A Gate 2 review found eight further pairs the join had missed, because it looked only at the register row's immediate DROP twin and not at the kept ledger row that twin points to; the same rule was applied to them (DR-039, DR-098, DR-103 and DR-147 are UNVERIFIED and became `DROP: duplicate of` a kept ledger row; VL-20-241, VL-23-535, VL-23-007 and VL-19-351 sit against a re-verified register row and became `DROP: duplicate of` it; table 8.1.3). Pairs that name no single kept ledger row, or that two Gate 2 reviewers read differently, were not changed and are listed in 8.1.4 limit 3b; a new full re-scan of every register/ledger pair was not made, so "one kept row" is claimed for the listed pairs, not for every defect in the file. Twin pairs were found by joining the register's `slice:line` cites to the ledgers' Source column, confirmed by the defect's own id token (for example D-12, X-3, P4) and read row by row; where a ledger row restates the defect with a different id the pair was added by hand from the register's crosswalk (file 17, "Open item (c)").

Cross-ledger duplicates (P3-011). Every group named by the reviewer was read in full and resolved to one destination: seal, hook, resume and session id (exchange layer) is CORE as an optional capability; tier and roster data, packaged panel templates and panel-resolution tests are CORE; the merged-report renderer is CORE (reviser wording stays a MODULE-spec plug-in); telemetry strata are CORE; the judge skip rule is HARNESS; `_REF_TOKEN` (DR-007 and DR-061) is CORE with per-target syntax as a MODULE-tasklist plug-in. The decided-roster recommendations (VL-20-122 to VL-20-125, VL-20-143) stay MODULE-tasklist. Table 8.1.3 lists each group with its rows and outcome. Besides these groups a read-only scan of the 3,989 rows that are not DROP for (a) identical statements across ledgers and (b) `file:line` cites shared by rows of different ledgers (a cite shared by more than six rows was skipped) found no identical statement and 29 cross-ledger pairs sharing at least one cite; the pairs were read and are different facts about the same file (none is the same item with two destinations), except VL-19-036 and VL-20-345 (same `/tmp` execution defect, both HARNESS, so no destination conflict). A full semantic comparison of all 5,779 ledger rows against each other was not done; the limits are listed in 8.1.4.

Provenance routing (P3-014). Every MODULE-tasklist row of ledgers 21 (214), 22 (124) and 20 (23) was read with its Reason column and re-judged by who would use the item, not by which study produced it. The recommended split used (research/09, research/10, research/12 Summaries and ledger 22 Summary item 2 and Gap Q3): the core keeps the finding contract, merge, ledger and verdict kernel, dispatch identity and the tier data, the brief slot for named evidence documents (H1) and anchor limits (H2), the card schema and the optional row block, counts-only telemetry, and the optional exchange layer (message envelope, board, hook delivery, seal, transport, deadline and hang guard); modules keep category, lens and ref sets, brief text, classes, extractors, catalogues, roles and schedules. Result: 70 rows moved (ledger 20: 9, ledger 21: 28, ledger 22: 30, ledger 23: 2, ledger 24: 1) to CORE or between modules, each with `moved from <old>: <why>` in its Reason column; the 278 MODULE-tasklist rows of ledgers 21 and 22 that stay carry the uniform tag `HOIST-CANDIDATE: spec, pr-review, rf-qa (...)`, and the five downward ties of ledger 23 and the four tie rows of ledger 24 (G-L7) carry `HOIST-CANDIDATE: CORE`. The MODULE rows of ledgers 19, 20, 23 and 24 whose Reason names CORE or another module (73 rows), every CORE row whose Reason names a single module (41 rows) and every CORE row whose Statement is about the reflect code or skill (67 rows) were also read; the checks moved one row from MODULE-reflect to CORE (VL-23-479, card path, with DR-146) and one row from CORE to MODULE-reflect (VL-24-181, whose own Reason calls it reflect prose); VL-23-629 (in-run enforcement of the contract key allowlist) stays CORE, its ledger destination, because DR-139 is UNVERIFIED and the ledger destination wins (only VL-23-618 is MODULE-reflect; the legal-key lists are reflect data, their enforcement is core code); VL-23-267 moved from EVAL to CORE with the telemetry strata (DR-022). Rows not named by one of these checks keep the ledger's own destination; they were not re-judged one by one (limit in 8.1.4).

For those pairs the ledger destination won by the rule in 8.1.1, so the register's Fix owner text for them sits only in the Reason column of the `DROP: duplicate of VL-NN-nnn` register row.

The exchange layer to CORE decision follows research/09 Summary and ledger 22 Gap Q3; it is a placement, not a quality claim: ledger 22 Summary item 1 states that no collaboration package has quality evidence and Question 1 of ledger 21 (does the unified panel include any reviewer-to-reviewer exchange) stays an owner decision. #### (d) Acceptance evidence a panel design needs

Status of these conditions: R16 Part 4 derives them from verified defects and verified gaps in the E1 and E2 efforts. They are research conclusions, not existing repository policy: R16 searched HEAD and found no document that defines acceptance for a panel (negative evidence; the only acceptance-like texts are the E1 `pilot-design.md` thresholds, the E1 `PLAN.md` lead rule, the E2 `PILOT-REPORT.md:56` rule and two unrun brainstorm decision rules). Each condition is stated so that a later plan can test it.

**Evidence tiers (R16 s4.2).** A panel design is accepted for a use case only when all three hold for that use case: Tier S (structural checks pass in code, no ground truth needed), Tier Q (quality on the derivation set meets a rule fixed before the run), Tier G (generalization: hold-out set, new packages, seeded defects with clean twins). Anything weaker is a lead, not a finding (E1 `PLAN.md:184`). Today Tier S exists for E1 (the exit script), Tier Q exists for E2 on three packages, and no Tier G evidence exists for any effort.

| # | Testable condition | Why (verified basis) |
|---|---|---|
| AE-1 | One ground-truth registry: every GT file has a recorded sha256, every item has a mechanical quote check (`quote_grep_count`, `evidence_ok`), and items that fail are listed under `dropped` with a reason. The recorded hash equals the hash at scoring time | E2 is the only effort with mechanical GT checks (16 items over 3 packages; designSpec GT sha256 `3e56551dc0046c9ff3f2e3f49fb2ccb82da8c63a8a781dbe13b0631ba8cb47e4`, makeTheAliasOnly `79e3205775deace4a9b02810f16abecca0fe3c11e256e8d79b6893df45f5eb1e`, control `e3585b8e6bf11241cdaafbf2faf5e52fd4c6dfed2176b1e7269b6a54c97d5a3c`, recomputed by R16). GT authorship (AI or human) is not recorded [UNVERIFIED]. R16 s3.1, s4.1 row 1 |
| AE-2 | Each use case has its own ground truth. Tasklist review: the E2 GT, as a derivation set only. Reflect UC-1 and UC-2, PR code review and rf-qa replacement: no GT exists today, so a seeded-defect or new implement-derived GT is required for each | R16 s4.3: E1 combo and pilot runs are all UC-1 pre; UC-2 never run; no GT file tracked at HEAD; E1 seeded-defect design (60 defects = 12 plans x 5) never run |
| AE-3 | The decision rule, the values file and the analysis script are committed before the first run commit, and the ordering is shown by `git log`, not by file mtimes. The script that produces the results table is the committed one | Every prose "pre-registered" rule reached git together with or after its data: E2 pilot rule (`PILOT-REPORT.md:54-58`) first appears in commit `b4db265a8` (2026-11-13 01:38 UTC) after the runs; E1 `PLAN.md:176-189` is ordered before the runs by mtime only and enters git in one commit `792cf8c52`. Only the code gate `scripts/reflect_shadow_exit.py` is verifiably pre-set. R16 s3.2 |
| AE-4 | Judge integrity is checked in code: judge model equals the requested model; the judge prompt hash and script hash are recorded per score; `score.json` exists, parses, has the schema keys the judge prompt requires, and its counts are consistent; the judge transcript or a digest is kept; a second judge on a sample uses a different model family | E2 `judge-one.sh` accepts a judge when `rc == 0` and `judge.json` parses (`:28-30`); it does not check `score.json`; a fabricated-looking `score.json` from a judge that died with an API error produced the retracted n2-sonnet-src score (`COMBO-REPORT.md:147`); the idempotence guard (`judge-one.sh:7`) never re-judges an existing file. The consistency identity `wrong_blockers = ledger_rows_blocking - blocking_rows_gt_matched` is read from audit-F by a slice and is [UNVERIFIED] here. R16 s1.2, s4.1 row 3 |
| AE-5 | Replicates vary the package, not only the reviewer draw. No single-run row enters a ranking. The report states a minimum detectable effect and the number of comparisons made | E2 runs r1 to r4 reuse the same three packages (pseudo-replication, `audit-F/flags.tsv:56`); family sd 0.94 on found mean 2.33; audit F counts about 48 tests (2 to 3 false positives expected at 0.05); exact two-sided permutation floors: 4 vs 4 is 2/C(8,4) = 0.0286, 4 vs 6 is 0.0095 (R16 re-derived). R16 s4.1 row 4 |
| AE-6 | An executable run verifier (R16 calls it `verify-run`) passes before any results table is produced, and "unaudited" is a reported state, never silent absence. Keys are exact tuples, never prefixes; the population comes from a manifest; severity (EXCLUDE or WARN) is owned by one policy file; the summary is printed from the flags, not hand-written | E2 defects: `fullpkg()` matches ids by a 12-character prefix, so 59 control-package EXCLUDE flags map to designSpec and 11 more exclude all three packages (committed 69 reproduced; corrected 71 to 76); `BAD_CHECKS` hand-selects which EXCLUDE ids count (`final-table.py:20`); six audits use different valid-era predicates; the audit-A summary disagrees with its own flags (930 vs 890 runs; 59 vs 54 WARN); batch j1 is in none of the six `flags.tsv` files (hand-audited by research/08 s6 with no identity or drop problem and two luna refusals, which does not change "not confirmed"). #### R1 8.1 Value inventory (b)

**How the inventory was built.** Every item list of the six scope slices and every finding, takeaway and gap of research files 01 to 13 was walked in order (slice 00 sections 1 to 9, slice 01 sections 1 to 6, slice 02 sections 1 to 8, slice 03 sections 1 to 7, slice 04 sections 0 to 7, slice 05 sections 1 to 6, then research 01 to 13, then the web files), followed by the 25 closed items (`GQ:C-01` to `GQ:C-25`) and the 77 contradicted or stale-doc rows (`GQ:D-01` to `GQ:D-77`), each of which has its own row (kept, dropped with a reason, or noted as corrected). The two effort columns of `gaps-and-questions.md` are not mixed: its "Effort" column is the studied effort (E1/E2/E3, combinations, `cross`) and its "Closure effort" column is R1-C1/R1-C2/R1-C3; this table's Effort column is the origin effort of the item.

### 8.4 Run 1 migration content
<!-- Variant 1 (modified) — V1:3829, 3860, 3879, 3897 (`**Dependencies:**`) deleted as ordering content; V1:3830, 3861, 3880, 3898 carried only in 8.6 (M-18); leading status column added (R25-INV-027) -->

Run 1's in-cell prerequisite notes are logical prerequisites as run 1 defines them at its 8.2 lead, not an order of work. The first column of each step table gives the step's status against the adopted design, copied from the fault-finder enumeration (R25-INV-027): 13 CONFLICTS, 14 PARTLY COMPATIBLE, 21 COMPATIBLE. The four `**Dependencies:**` lines of run 1's track introductions are dropped as ordering content, and its four persisted-format and rollback lines are carried only in 8.6. <!-- Source: new (lead per Change #M-16) -->

#### R1 8.2 Migration path

One subsection per migration track (labels fixed by the owner: R1-M1 shared-core contract; R1-M2 reflect onto core; R1-M3 tasklist and spec consumers; R1-M4 future consumers). Step ids (`M1-01` and so on) only name steps so that gaps can point at them; they carry no order, date or sprint. "Depends on" names logical prerequisites (a step cannot be verified without them), not a sequence. Names marked [proposed] do not exist in code. The steps that touch the core verdict word set (R1-M1-07, R1-M1-08, R1-M1-16, R1-M3-08) carry the synth-05 `[CONTRADICTION]` (core verdict vocabulary: PENDING and exit 12 under `--decide grader` against an unattended non-PASS defaulting to ESCALATE with no new exit code, R1-OD-8) as an open item and do not resolve it. R1-M4-05 depends on R1-M1-16 and inherits the open item through that dependency; R1-M2-02 and R1-M2-10 touch only reflect's own 1.8.0 verdict mapping (module side: four verdicts, `merge_method`, the verdict file), not the core word set, so they do not carry the flag. Paths are repository paths under `src/superclaude/` unless written otherwise; installed primitives reach the CLI through the `superclaude` command, never through `src/superclaude/` paths.

##### Track R1-M1: shared-core contract

**Goal:** one finding contract, one clusterer, one merge-and-verdict stage, one run record, one resolver and one brief renderer in `src/superclaude/cli/review/`, so that a new lens is added by data and a thin module (R1-SC-14), and the sixteen defects R1-D1..R1-D16 are fixed once.

### 8.5 Run 1 no-regression gates

Run 1's 19 gates carry the prefix `R1-`: R1-G1..R1-G11, R1-G-all, R1-G-bench, R1-G-exit, R1-G-new, R1-G-pr, R1-G-replay, R1-G-skills and R1-G-sync. Run 2's gates G1-G27 keep their own numbers, and every gate cross-reference in run 2's constraints (C19-C27) and gates (G17-G22) means run 2 numbering (R25-INV-018). The "Must NOT change" pins of R1-G2 on `test_review_ledger.py:299-304` and `:468-472` are conditional on run 1's verdict design, which is not adopted; they belong on the rewrite list of run 2's C18 (R25-INV-026). <!-- Source: new (lead per Change #M-17) -->

### 8.6 Run 1 persisted-format compatibility and rollback rules

Run 1's persisted-format and rollback rules from its four track introductions (V1:3830 for R1-M1, V1:3861 for R1-M2, V1:3880 for R1-M3, V1:3898 for R1-M4); they are carried only here, not in 8.4. <!-- Source: new (lead per Change #M-18) -->

**Persisted formats and rollback (applies to every R1-M1 step; [proposed] rule, not in code).** Each persisted format keeps its schema string until a deliberate bump (`review-ledger/1`, `review-panel-manifest/1`, `review-telemetry/1`): new keys are optional; files written before the step are read without migration; `validate` and `load` accept both the old and the new form; and the step's tests re-validate recorded artifacts (the step rows name them). Rollback: each step is one change that can be reverted alone; a revert leaves files that hold the new optional keys, so every step that adds a persisted key also adds a test that the previous reader tolerates unknown keys (whether it does today is [UNVERIFIED] for `ledger.load` and `manifest.load` until that test exists). The track-level rollback line is: revert in reverse dependency order, run R1-G1 to R1-G11 and R1-G-exit, and confirm the 13 recorded shadow manifests still validate.

**Rollback (R1-M2; [proposed] rule).** Contract 1.8.0 stays byte-identical in every R1-M2 step except the R1-M2-10 bump gate, so reverting a step leaves recorded shadow runs and their contracts valid; after a revert run R1-G8 and R1-G-exit (the recorded shadow runs must still count 13 of 20 with the same failures); an edit to `SKILL.md` outside the R1-C6 allowed sections is reverted together with its R1-C6 allowed-list change.

**Rollback (R1-M3; [proposed] rule).** R1-M3-03 to R1-M3-06 change the post-gate engine only and keep its CLI line, exit codes, output files and the `reflect_post:` block, so a revert restores today's behaviour (the blocking gate cannot HALT, R1-ENS-1) and R1-G9 must stay green; R1-M3-01, R1-M3-02, R1-M3-08 and R1-M3-09 are text and test edits whose pins are in R1-G10, R1-G11 and R1-G-skills and whose plugin copies are reverted with them.

**Rollback (R1-M4; [proposed] rule).** Adding a lens entry or a thin module is additive, so a revert removes the entry and its tests; the router change of R1-M4-03 is reverted together with its R1-G-pr test changes; the rf-qa pins moved by R1-M4-06 are restored with the files they cover (R1-G10).

**Correction (R25-INV-003).** "Keep the schema string and add optional keys" is safe only for additive changes. V2's adopted ledger design changes clearing and verdict semantics, which run 1's own debate (R1-C13-22 R1-INV-014, V1:2657) closed with a `min_writer` field and a `review-ledger/2` bump; an old installed binary would clear rows by silence on a new ledger and raise `KeyError` on `last["verdict"]` (`ledger.py:363-372`). This is an open decision with both versions: <!-- Source: new (correction per Change #M-18, R25-INV-003) -->

- V2 (A-9): keep `review-ledger/1`. <!-- Source: new (M-18) -->
- Run 1 (R1-C13-22 R1-INV-014, V1:2657): a `min_writer` field plus the `review-ledger/2` bump. <!-- Source: new (M-18) -->

### 8.7 Run 1 branch-structure constraint and facts (options table dropped, M-19)
<!-- Variant 1 (modified) — heading V1:4057 "### 8.4 Branch-structure options" replaced per M-19; options table V1:4063-4069 (layouts A-E) dropped as a branch plan -->

Run 1's five-layout options table (V1:4063-4069) is a branch plan and is not carried; the git constraint and the facts are. <!-- Source: new (lead per Change #M-19) -->

**Git constraint (applies to every layout that uses a slash).** `feat/review-panel` and `feat/review-panel/<name>` cannot both exist: a ref name cannot be both a branch and a directory of branches, because git stores `refs/heads/feat/review-panel` as a file and `refs/heads/feat/review-panel/<name>` needs a directory of the same name. A layout therefore either has an umbrella branch `feat/review-panel` with children named without a slash after `review-panel` (for example `feat/review-panel-m1-core`), or has namespaced children `feat/review-panel/<name>` with no branch called `feat/review-panel`.

**The constraint in both reports and for the owner's prefix.** Both reports state it: `feat/review-panel` and `feat/review-panel/<name>` cannot both exist, in either creation order (run 1 above; run 2 C4, V2:4433). Applied to the owner's chosen prefix: no branch named `feat_review-panel` may exist (local, packed or remote-tracking) while any `feat_review-panel/<name>` exists; both names are valid alone per `git check-ref-format`; no such refs exist locally or on origin (fault-finder row 31). <!-- Source: new (constraint restatement per Change #M-19) -->

**Facts that shape the options** (all from the research files; ownership is owner item R1-O-4, R1-G-92): the `cli/review` package on this branch equals `origin/master`, so the E1 kernel is master code after #519 and the branch `ironbelly/shadow-runs` is 5 commits past merge-base `d2d8a2d16` (`origin/master` `d4d1662a8` is 3 commits past the merge-base), touching only `SKILL.md`, `refs/reviewer-spec.md`, two reflect tests and documents (`research/09` section 1.1; GQ:R1-D-72); the local `master` ref is stale, so any new branch is cut from `origin/master` (project rule: fetch and rebase onto `origin/master` before pushing); PRs go only to the fork `IronbellyOrg/IronClaude` through `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3`, never to the upstream; worktrees are created through Orca with an agent; `.claude/` mirrors are never staged and `.dev/tasks/` is always staged; the reflect pins R1-C1, R1-C6, R1-C14 compare with HEAD, so changes to the reflect skill text are kept in separate commits from changes to the pinned sections and R1-G8 is run before each commit; the live7 test couples `review-tiers.default.json` to `ccsession-models.json`, so tier edits and that file change in one PR (GQ:R1-G-90); both panel goldens regenerate on any tier-file byte change, so two branches that edit the tier file or the resolution record conflict. The rollback unit in every layout is one merged PR, so layouts C and D revert all the steps they merged together (the rollback lines of 8.2 and the persisted-format rule of the R1-M1 intro apply). This section states layouts and trade-offs only; it commits to no order, date or sprint. <!-- Variant 1 (modified) — M-19 / M-25: stale '3 commits ahead' -->

### 9.11 Run 1 open questions

**Source key.** `Gnn` = gap row nn of `gaps-and-questions.md` section 1; `Dnn` = row nn of its section 2; `Onn` = owner item of its section 3; `Cnn` = closed item of its section 4. `NN` = `research/NN-*.md`. Effort tags: E1 = reflect Tier 2 panel and shadow mode (branch `ironbelly/shadow-runs`); E2 = tasklist review-panel evaluation study at the E2 commit above; E3 = #346 review loop on master plus installed-only experiment variants. Closure effort: R1-C1 = no new work (the report carries it from existing evidence), R1-C2 = small read-only check, R1-C3 = new research, a measured run or an input only the owner or another session can supply.

In this merged copy, these ids carry the prefix `R1-` (Merge Notes, id rule). <!-- Source: new (legend line, rule 3) -->

In this block `R1-Gn` means gap row n and `R1-C1` to `R1-C3` mean closure effort (V1:4126); closed items carry `R1-CLS-nn`. <!-- Source: new (9.11 id note, rule 3) -->

**Severity.** Under the gap-log rating no gap is Critical (both cross-validation and both gap-detection reports state that none blocks synthesis). 30 gaps are Important; all 30 appear below as their own question or as a named part of one (rows R1-Q-01 to R1-Q-30). All 64 Minor gaps appear in rows R1-Q-05, R1-Q-02 or R1-Q-31 to R1-Q-44.

Gap-log rating: 94 gaps, 0 Critical, 30 Important, 64 Minor. Section 4 re-rates 15 rows Critical and 66 Important (the 15 Critical rows are 11 distinct gaps: 7 under control R1-C8, 4 on impact, see Section 4.1 row 15); both counts are used, each with its basis, and Section 9 follows the gap-log rating.

Row labels: [Required] = a question the task requires in this table; [Owner] = from AMBIGUITIES_FOR_USER; [Important] = an Important gap not already listed; [Minor group] = Minor gaps grouped by theme (each gap ID named); [Web] = an UNVERIFIED item from the web research files; [Debate] = an open decision or unaddressed invariant left by one of the four adversarial debates or by the QA gate (rows R1-Q-47 to R1-Q-61, Section 9.5; these rows carry no gap ID). A gap that appears in a [Required] row is not repeated elsewhere. Section 9.1 maps every gap ID to its question row.

| Topic | Files | Side used and why |

| Whether batch j1 is an unexamined hole | R16 (first version) against R08 s6 | R08: it hand-audited all 45 j1 runs and ran a six-scenario sensitivity table; R16 adopted it in fix cycle 1 |
| Whether location type is a core blocker | R13 (first conclusion) against R01 (probe P-a, C-3) and R17 (DR-113) | R01 and R17: executed reproduction; R13 corrected in fix cycle 1 (mechanism refined by Gate 1: v1 `parse_block` already requires `anchor`; `annotate` raises when a v2-validated citations-only finding reaches it directly) |
| Status of D-17 and D-23 | R17 (DR-117, DR-121 UNVERIFIED) against R15 s2-3 (reproduced) | R15: scratch execution and deterministic interleaving; limit: no real two-process race run, no incident in 29 manifests |
| `identity_source` in contracts | scope slice 11 (as relayed) against R04 s4.2 | R04: counted from the 15 combo and 13 pilot contracts |
| Whether engine A's diversity fields come from SERVED or REQUESTED `model_id` | R06 s2.5, s5.4 ("SERVED worker `model_id` values") against R04 s3.3, s4.1 | R04: code read (`openai_compat.py:467-470`, `model_id=self._model`; `_diversity.py:8-15` counts distinct `worker.model_id`) plus a negative grep (the response `model` field is never read); R06's wording rests on a slice with no code line |
